text.text:
We enjoyed the beach the most during our stay. It’s long, wide, and covered with beautiful, soft white sand — truly a highlight of the property. The hotel also has a large swimming pool, which is a great place for guests to relax.

Another thing we enjoyed was the animal visits on Sundays. The small, gentle animals were very cute and made the experience fun for everyone, especially for kids and taking photos.

Our room was comfortable and had a great view. However, there was an incident involving a housekeeping staff member that unfortunately caused some disappointment during our stay.

The restaurant was decent, though not particularly memorable. One small detail we noticed was that Ritz properties usually refresh personal care amenities daily, but at this hotel they were only provided on the first day unless requested.

The small cookie and candy jars on the table are a nice gesture, though it felt a bit surprising that they were charged as extra items considering the premium price of the stay.

Overall, we had some enjoyable aspects of the visit, especially the beach and pool, but there are a few areas where the experience could be improved.

text.text:
A Disappointing Anniversary: Inconsistent Service & Poor Management

We stayed for 2 nights for our anniversary, and while there were highlights, this property is showing its age and lacks the basic standards of the Ritz-Carlton brand.

The Room & Housekeeping (The "Ugly"):
The hotel is dated and, frankly, one of the least attractive Ritz properties we’ve seen. We were upgraded to a 1-bedroom suite, but it was filthy. There was dust and someone else’s makeup under the TV stand that stayed there our entire stay. We complained on the first night, but the Housekeeping Manager didn't return our call until 5 minutes before we checked out on Day 3. What can you even do at that point?

Service Failures:
* Check-in: A staff member pulled a newly arrived guest to the front of a long line because they "just got off a flight" (as did the rest of us). A pathetic offer of water didn't fix the frustration.
* Anniversary: Promised champagne/strawberries took 3 follow-ups and 2 days to arrive.
* Pool: Service is slow; we were completely ignored while staff handed out fruit to everyone else.
* Spa: Short-staffed and unable to accommodate us. I appreciate that they called multiple times a day to give us staffing updates, but a hotel of this caliber should be prepared.

Dining & The "Good":
* Club Lounge: The standout of the trip. Amazing service and great F&B selection. This is the only place that felt like a Ritz.
* The Beach: Slow service, but the fish tacos and guacamole were incredible.
* Zaytinya: Overpriced and mediocre. Good cocktails, but disappointing for a Jose Andres spot.
* Room Service: The breakfast attendant was amazing and the food was great (though $14 for 2 eggs with no toast is a bit much).

The Verdict:
The 20% automatic service charge seems to have removed any incentive for the staff to provide actual "luxury" service. Aside from the Club Lounge and the beach food, this was a major letdown.

Downgraded Without Notice on Valentine’s Day — Completely Unacceptable Experience

Our Valentine’s Day stay at The Ritz-Carlton South Beach was a complete disappointment.

We booked one month in advance, a balcony with a view room yet upon arrival our room was downgraded without any notice or consent to a no view window room. As Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite members, we expected professionalism and transparency. Instead, we were placed in Room 506 facing a rooftop full of AC units. There was no view whatsoever — we couldn’t see the ocean, the city, or even a street. In South Beach, surrounded by water and beautiful scenery, being placed in a room where you can’t even tell where you are is unacceptable. The room felt horrible and completely below expectations.

Even worse, no one contacted us proactively, and customer service made no real effort to correct the situation after we reached out several times.

This was supposed to be a special Valentine’s celebration, and instead it turned into stress and disappointment.

Do not trust reservations at this property if the experience and basic respect for your booking matter to you. DO NOT BOOK THIS HOTEL ON SPECIAL DATES OR BUSY TIMES IN MIAMI BEACHo. This hotel failed to deliver the level of service expected from the Ritz-Carlton name.

text.text:
Just checked in for the next 2 nights and wanted to leave a practical note for other travellers—mainly so expectations match the product.

Positives so far: Front desk staff has been polite, calm, and responsive. When we raised the issue below, they gave a clear explanation without being dismissive.

Key concern (functionality, not aesthetics): The guestroom lighting is very limited. There is no ceiling light and the room relies largely on a small number of lamps. Even with every light switched on, the overall brightness is still low. That matters because lighting isn’t just “ambience”—it affects basic room usability (reading, working on a laptop, packing, finding items, and getting ready at night).

We asked frontdesk staff Mark whether a brighter room was available, and were told this is the design/theme across the hotel and there were no alternative options. He diligently sent an engineer to ensure the existing 2 lamps are working.

Who this will suit: If you prefer a dim, moodier aesthetic and don’t plan to do much in-room, you may be fine.

Who should think twice: If you value practical, well-lit rooms (families, people working while travelling, anyone needing clear lighting), factor this in before booking.

Overall: Reasonable staff and straightforward communication, but the lighting setup significantly reduces day-to-day comfort and room functionality for us.

11.1.2026

Thank you for the reply, Giancarlo.

For clarity for anyone reading: this was not about a preference for “mood lighting” or aesthetics—it was about basic room functionality. Our guestroom had no ceiling light and relied on a small number of lamps; even with all lights on, overall brightness remained low, which materially affected practical tasks (packing, reading, working on a laptop, finding items, and getting ready at night).

Your response notes you “regret we did not meet your expectations regarding the lighting,” but does not confirm whether this lighting setup is standard across the property, nor what specific corrective action is planned. That distinction matters because it helps future guests understand whether this is an isolated room issue or a consistent hotel-wide feature.

For transparency: we raised it at check-in. Front desk were polite and responsive and advised this was the design/theme across the hotel with no brighter alternative available; an engineer attended and confirmed the existing lamps were functioning.

If this is being “addressed,” it would be helpful to outline what concrete change is being considered (e.g., additional lamps, brighter fittings/bulbs, or identifying rooms with higher task-lighting), and whether guests who need a well-lit room can request this in advance.

Posted in good faith: staff were reasonable. My aim is simply to help other travellers—especially families and those working while travelling—make an informed choice.

text.text: Like 👍🏼 our review! We had a wonderful overnight stay at Albion South Beach Hotel in Miami Beach, Florida after flying into Fort Lauderdale to depart for our cruise the next day. We chose the place due to its solid reviews, walking distance to Lincoln Road shopping area and beaches, and great value for the price point. Overall, the hotel met our expectations and we really enjoyed the cozy bedroom with four pillows, clean bathroom with a tub, large closet and safe for valuables, reasonable internet speed for emails and searching, beautiful and comfortable lobby, quiet hallways for a good sleep, a small working gym, free morning coffee (after 7AM) on the mezzanine, and most importantly, a kind and personable staff. Please note that we didn't have access to the pool since it's currently being renovated during our stay and it was not a problem to us. Since we were on the third floor, it was very easy to take the stairs instead of the slow elevator. However, we enjoyed the access to a sleek bar downstairs for a late night drink and access to an a ala carte breakfast with a variety of offerings. Lastly, the hotel offered a luggage hold for the day allowing us to explore the area more before departing for the cruise. Given this, we would love to stay here again and would definitely recommend this place to our friends and family.

text.text: The Sagamore is an interesting conundrum - on the positive side, the beach access is great. The free chairs and towels are also nice (although I think this is fairly standard for a beach-adjacent hotel). The service was also prompt as in people responded or showed up quickly when requested. However, for a hotel that is supposedly “4 stars”, here’s what I think was lacking: first - the rooms are a bit odd, definitely not “4 stars”. They are dated and sparse - very little in the way of amenities or even furniture. The “beach view” I had was actually just a view to adjacent concrete building with spray painted writing all over it (which was made more comical when I got an email after my stay asking me to rate my “beach view room”). Second - the cleaning was a bit lackluster. The room did not seem overly “clean” from the get go and when we had it cleaned, the tile floors always had hair remaining on them or sand. The bathroom never felt particularly clean and the table and chairs had stains and marks all over them. They also left a dirty cleaning rag on top of my wife’s cosmetics case and hairbrush the last day we were there. Further, each day the staff seemed to want to get out of cleaning our room and seemed like they were trying to get me to confirm I didn’t need cleaning each day in the morning when they came by. Third, the walls were like paper - there was constant noise from late evening to early morning and honestly it could by hard to sleep through it. Not to mention, there seemed to be ongoing construction at the hotel or building next door and we had no forewarning. One day my wife went to open the blinds in the morning and there were several construction workers standing right outside our 2nd floor window.  Fourth, the room has a wet bar / kitchen set up but it is completely devoid of any dishes or silverware. It was noted that you can request it, which I did, and was told I could have plastic utensils and plastic plates. That is all fine, but again, not a 4-star hotel experience. For context, I have stayed in probably 100+ hotels all over the world ranging from 3-5 star so I think I have a good sample of what 4-star in the USA generally looks/feels like. Overall, the experience felt like a lower end 3 star hotel trying to stretch to obtain a 4 star rating while  spending the least amount of money on renovations and amenities to actually deliver a 4 star experience.

text.text:
Unfortunately, staying here wasn't the greatest experience. First and foremost, there was never any hot water. It did get mildly warm for ~2/20 showers during my 10 day stay. Enduring icy showers every day, however, was not the best.

The air conditioning barely worked, leaving me sweating in my room all night. I had to go out and buy USB fans just to sleep comfortably. Adjusting the thermostat didn’t seem to make a difference at all, I wondered if it was even connected to anything.

The TV setup was a letdown as well. There’s no HDMI port or smart TV features, so I couldn’t connect any of my devices or watch anything at all during my entire stay. When I searched behind the TV for an HDMI port, I was met with a really thick layer of sticky dust—it was quite unappealing to dig through to look for a port. I figured it was standard for most hotels to have at least one hdmi port available, without it the TV is just useless wall decor.

On the subject of cleanliness, the overall condition of my room was pretty poor. There were actual visible dust clumps everywhere: on the walls, lamps, and even in the fridge, others were hanging off fixtures and from the ceiling. It was really pretty gross and looked like the room hadn't been cleaned thoroughly in months or years. Most of the appliances were broken or had other issues, and the towel bar and bathroom mirror were starting to fall off the wall.

You could hear everything from the upstairs guests, somehow even their phones vibrating on a table. While this noise alone from neighbors wouldn't have been that big of an issue, the noise from the cleaning staff slamming doors nonstop throughout the day, seemingly as hard as they could, and starting daily around **6 AM**, made it difficult to get quality sleep or enjoy any kind of sleep in on your vacation. I noticed others complaining about outside external noise in reviews, but I found that to be expected in South Beach and wasn’t particularly bothered by it.

On the brighter side, the rooms were a decent size and furnished well. The bed was comfortable, and the limited staff interactions I had were very friendly and helpful every time. The location is good, and the pool area was really very nice.

A heads-up: the front door locks at night, and staff isn’t always at the front desk. My key cards stopped working one day, so if I hadn't forgotten something and had to go back to my room in the morning, I could have easily been locked out that night.

In short, while there were some positive aspects to my stay, and while it certainly wasn't *terrible*, these issues really overshadowed my experience, particularly the lack of A/C, hot water, and the all-day door slamming. I’ve stayed at several other hotels on Collins with much better experiences.

Our room was nice and clean, view was great besides the floor to ceiling windows being dirty on the outside. TV did not work and neither did the in-suite phone. First time I came to Lowes and with excitment because i thought its luxury hotel. Beautiful people at front desk, I agree.

Umbrellas for the beach are extra they would not provide that but yes you will have chairs and towells…I had no idea about this either. So my take on this is dont waste your money here. Its not worth it.

text.text:
Stayed for the weekend. The decor was lovely, with vintage photographs on the walls and dark flooring that added old-world charm. The bathroom was beautiful, and the bed was comfortable. The staff were very kind and genuinely tried to help and resolve any issues. Breakfast was a nice touch — good coffee, eggs with potatoes, and a super friendly server. There’s even a partial ocean view from the rooftop deck, and the location is great — an easy walk to everything.

However, this property does not feel like a true 4-star hotel, and it’s unclear why it carries the Curio brand, especially when compared to the Hotel del Coronado. We were disappointed to find that the main restaurant facing Collins Street was under construction — we had been looking forward to relaxing there after our days out. The lounge on the other side was closed as well, and even the front coffee bar wasn’t open. We were not informed about the remodeling when we booked well in advance.

Our room had a spacious patio, but the daybed needed cleaning. My side of the bed had no nightstand, and overall, the room could have used a deep clean. Unfortunately, the value didn’t match the experience.

Thank you anyway, and best of luck to the team.

I will never ever recommend this hotel to anyone and definitely will not be back… No fridge nor microwave either. That have a wine fridge.

text.text:
The location of this hotel is great a lot of shops, stores, places to eat within walking distance and the beach is just a short drive.

The hotel offers parking, however, it’s coned off and you are responsible for moving the cones to get in and out of the parking lot. In addition, they demand that you to give them your car keys while you are at the hotel. They didn’t ask politely or even explain why they literally demand you hand over your car keys if you are present at the hotel. They have a man during the day that looks homeless who literally will chase you if you don’t turn in the car keys. This was very odd to me. On our 3rd night we needed more toilet paper. Upon asking the front desk for more comments we’re made that the people who give out the tissue leave at 4 and if you need toilet paper you should not have your “do not disturb” sign up. 0 hospitality. The rooms were very basic, beds were thin, pillows thin, had to keep playing around with the ac to make sure it stayed on. The room had a microwave and a mini fridge inside the same closet where you hang your clothes. So if you warm up food your clothes will smell like it. Not worth the price even with having a great location. I would never re-book or recommended this place.

text.text:
One might expect to have a peaceful and relaxing stay in a hotel, particularly in South Beach; however, my experience at the James Hotel in Miami, FL, was quite the opposite.

I arrived at approximately 3:30 PM on December 13, 2025, hoping to receive my room thirty minutes prior to the 4:00 PM check-in time (Confirmation # 9078866105381, initials J.A.).

The receptionist, who introduced herself as the "daughter of the hotel's owner," informed me she would impose a $10 fee for storing my bag, even for a few minutes, a $10 fee for "early" parking, and a $50 fee for early check-in. Interestingly, the lobby was empty, there was only one car in the parking lot, and it was only a few minutes before the check-in time of 4:00 PM. Furthermore, she mentioned a $50 per hour charge for late check-out. Her condescending and harsh demeanor was clearly intended to intimidate me, ultimately ruining my weekend.

While I understand hotels have their policies, this kind of rude behavior towards a paying guest is unacceptable and not a proper way to conduct business.

This individual's inappropriate behavior and condescending attitude are intolerable. Guests should not be treated in such a manner. It is particularly concerning as she claimed to be the "daughter of the owner" and threatened to cancel my reservation when I inquired about her name, which she refused to provide.

Although the room rate was relatively modest and the additional charges minimal, I see no reason to patronize this hotel.t is a fact that the hospitality industry is struggling and having a difficult time coping. I don't like writing negative reviews --- but, this is something that everybody should  know about.

Thank goodness AMEX Travel was able to cancel my booking and helped me through this ordeal.

Lastly, this James Hotel doesn't even look like it has clean & nice rooms since everything seems deary from the outside and at the lobby.

I decided to take the next flight back to NYC since I cannot possibly stay in South Beach with this unsettling experience in my mind.

Air conditioning doesn't work and manager by far the rudest woman I've met.

Air conditioning didn't work in our initial room and asked for this to be looked at the next day. Reception staff were kind and helpful and said they would see to it. We got back later that evening and the room was exactly the same temperature. So went back to reception and again receptionist was helpful and provided us with an extra room (next to the original room).

Obviously the new room was extremely hot as it hadn't had the air conditioning running whatsoever so given the late hour I decided to move my belongings across to the new room and try to sleep as the room cooled. The new room didn't cool and I woke up drenched in sweat. My original room was still cooler than the new one so I went to try and sleep in there instead as it was now 4.00 in the morning.

The manager then woke me and my partner up SHOUTING that we leave the room. I explained the situation and the manager did not apologize for her tone or the condition of the room. She was totally out of order and even when she had calmed herself down did not apologize for her tone when talking to me or my partner.

We truly tired to be understanding about the condition of the room and I would not have left a negative review had the manager now been totally out of order. We cancelled our future booking for that hotel and I would urge you to do the same.

The newly renovated Delano Hotel would be our go to hotel now at the Miami Beach area. The location is amazing, the pool was spectacular and the beach front was beautiful. The rooms, and amenities were done meticulously and I highly recommend staying here.

Not that those are enough reasons to stay here but don’t forget about the amazing team members who will take care of you during your stay. Some names to mention, Jeremy at the pool bar, Tanya at the pool, Ethan and Thomas at the beach. Each and every team member of the Delano will make sure that you are well attended to. The people who helped us out took our stay to the next level!!

We will be back and look forward to staying here again.

Also don’t forget to check out the restaurant on the 4th floor, Mimi Kakushi. The best and most creative drinks in town! And the food is amazing too!

text.text:
We stayed at the building, called Davis for at least three nights. As soon as we walked into our building, the elevator was out of order, when we stepped into our room, I noticed there were chocolate smudges in an area of the floor. I thought no biggie the following morning. I woke up to realize that there was also chocolate smudged on my sheets, I raise this concern to the front lobby and they put in a request to switch my sheets, when I came back, they were switched. Then our first night here the Wi-Fi was out when I brought it up to the front lobby. They were very rude and told us they were working on it. It was fixed the next day.
If you’re planning to eat out and want to bring your leftovers with you, I would advise you not to, the fridge only stays cold for two hours, and there are no microwaves anywhere. Our bathroom was very small. The toilet was nearly touching the wall and there is no ventilation in the bathroom.
I will give credit to the outside area. It is very nice and there are lots of seatings. The pool though is very small, but that is not a big deal as there is a beach two blocks away.
You definitely get what you pay for and nothing more when booking this hotel.

I’m not quite sure how I feel about this hotel. When we first arrived, I was impressed by the exterior and the pool area, it looked really nice and gave a great first impression. However, once we received our room, I was very disappointed.

One of the main reasons we chose this hotel was because the listing clearly stated that the room had two washrooms. When we arrived, the room only had one bathroom for our double queen booking plus sofa pull out bed. When we raised this issue with the staff, we were told there was nothing they could do, which was extremely frustrating since this incorrect information directly influenced our decision to book the property.

Additionally, the cleanliness of the room was unacceptable. The room appeared dirty and poorly maintained, which made our stay very uncomfortable. The sofa bed was especially concerning, it had visible stains and looked so unhygienic that we didn’t feel comfortable using it at all. Because of this, our group of six had to squeeze three people onto each bed.

For a property listed on Expedia, we expected a much higher standard of cleanliness and accuracy in the listing. Overall, the experience felt very misleading and disappointing.

text.text:
I stayed at the hotel for a week with my fiancé. Until checkout, we were genuinely happy with our stay, so much so that I even encouraged a friend to book a room there as well. Unfortunately, the way the hotel handled a simple lost item completely changed my impression.

After checking out on Saturday morning, we left our luggage at the hotel as our flight was later that evening. Around two hours after checkout, I realised I had left a shirt hanging on the bathroom door hook. My fiancé immediately called the hotel, but the call was disconnected…tried to call minimum 5 times after that - no answer.

When we returned to collect our luggage, I informed reception about the item. The staff member immediately stated that nothing had been found - without checking. Only after I insisted did she go to speak with housekeeping. She then returned and repeated that nothing had been found.

I am absolutely certain where I left the shirt. While it had little monetary value, it was a sentimental souvenir from travels. What is most disappointing is not the loss itself, but the dismissive and unprofessional way the situation was handled. There was no genuine attempt to assist, no empathy, and no accountability.

It is frustrating to leave what was otherwise a pleasant stay with the feeling that concerns are dismissed rather than properly addressed. Unfortunately, this experience has significantly affected my overall impression of the hotel.

That said, what truly made our stay exceptional was Ada, the morning shift receptionist. Her service was outstanding and genuinely made our experience so much better. She was always kind, attentive, and incredibly helpful, often going above and beyond what was expected. It’s rare to come across someone who cares this much about guests, and it really shows in everything she does.

Thanks to Ada, our stay was memorable. We would absolutely stay here again and highly recommend this hotel, especially because of the amazing service we received.

Unacceptably bad experience here. Hard to imagine it’s labeled as a 4-star hotel. Both my wife and I got allergic reactions. We sneezed a lot, and my wife got tearing and swollen eyes and also red spots on her skin. Our friends got sore throat and coughing. Not sure what exactly caused these, but we smelled mold in our friends’ room on 3rd floor and strong smell of fragrance in our room on 2nd floor. I guess the fragrance is used to cover up the smell of mold. We all got rid of these allergic symptoms after leaving the hotel for a day.

Other issues: sweat smell from the bed, small room, loud A/C, mandatory amenity fees, and far distance to parking garage.

Front desk is friendly and helpful. But understandably they can do nothing about these.

P.S. We also stayed in some under-maintained Airbnb in Miami but even that doesn’t cause us any allergic symptoms.

I would strongly advise others to avoid this place.

I stayed at this hotel for four days and, honestly, I wouldn't come back. From the first day the stairs were completely dark. There was no light working and every time I had to go up or down, I had to turn on the phone's flashlight so I wouldn't fall. It is unacceptable for a hotel to allow something so dangerous.

The TV control didn't work either and the screen froze. The dishes in the kitchen were also dirty.

Overall, the experience was disappointing. I expected basic conditions of security and functionality, but this place did not comply with any of that. I don't recommend it.

text.text:
Overall: solid 3.5 stars

The good:
•	Location is perfect. You’re one block from the beach and in the middle of everything.
•	Service was genuinely excellent. Check-in with Melody was great, she was friendly, welcoming, and went out of her way to get us into a room early. We arrived on a morning flight fully expecting to wait until the official check-in time, so being able to shower and reset right away was a big deal.
•	Amenities are impressive for South Beach. Beach towels and chairs, bikes for rent, gym passes, water, coffee, etc. Not every hotel in the area offers that without nickel-and-diming.
•	Housekeeping was solid. Daily cleanup, nicely refreshed room, and bottled water (oddly 2 out of 3 days but still appreciated).
•	Bathroom was great. Spacious shower and good water pressure.

What needs work:
•	Noise insulation is basically non-existent. Besides the usual Ocean Drive evening noise, our room was directly above a bar that blasted repetitive music with the same beat over and over- enough to drive anyone insane when you’re trying to sleep. At minimum they should offer proper earplugs for families or light sleepers.
•	Rooms are on the smaller side (fine for a couple, tight for a family of 3), and the layout is odd. There’s a little entry area separated by doors from the sleeping space, which is nice, but then there’s a transparent glass wall between that area and the shower. With a teenage daughter, it meant constantly watching who was going where while someone was showering or using the restroom.
•	We were placed in the building next door, not the main hotel building. To reach our room we had to walk through the “Naked Taco” restaurant, which takes up the entire lobby. The smell inside that lobby was honestly awful: a mix of throw-up, spilled liquor, and sewage. All three of us commented on it every single time. The main building lobby smelled fine, so I wish we’d been placed there instead. They really need to address the ventilation/cleanliness because no hotel guest wants that.
•	Pool is just okay. Nice to have, but only 3 ft deep and feels more like a bar/drinking scene than an actual pool where adults can swim or relax.

Bottom line:
Great location, great staff, surprisingly good amenities for South Beach, but noise, layout quirks, and that awful restaurant smell hold it back. If we stayed again, we’d only do it with a room in the main building and away from the bar

•	We were placed in the building next door, not the main hotel building. To reach our room we had to walk through the “Naked Taco” restaurant, which takes up the entire lobby. The smell inside that lobby was honestly awful: a mix of throw-up, spilled liquor, and sewage. All three of us commented on it every single time. The main building lobby smelled fine, so I wish we’d been placed there instead. They really need to address the ventilation/cleanliness because no hotel guest wants that.
•	Pool is just okay. Nice to have, but only 3 ft deep and feels more like a bar/drinking scene than an actual pool where adults can swim or relax.

Bottom line:
Great location, great staff, surprisingly good amenities for South Beach, but noise, layout quirks, and that awful restaurant smell hold it back. If we stayed again, we’d only do it with a room in the main building and away from the bar

I stayed for a few nights at Casa Boutique Hotel on Washington Avenue, and my overall experience was mixed but honest.

First off, the location is really convenient — it’s only a short walk from the beach and close to lots of restaurants and places I wanted to check out, which made it easy to get around without needing a car. The hotel itself has a clean, modern vibe in a small-scale, boutique kind of way, and the staff I interacted with were friendly and helpful.

My room was comfortable enough, though it felt a bit on the small side and didn’t have a lot of extra features (no pool or gym on site, for example). The continental breakfast and the fact that it’s included with the resort fee was a nice convenience, even if it wasn’t anything fancy. One thing I noticed was that because it’s right in the heart of South Beach, street noise was noticeable at night — something to keep in mind if you’re a light sleeper.

Overall, I’d say it’s a good budget-friendly choice if you want to be close to the beach and nightlife without spending too much, but it’s not a place you’d stay at if you’re looking for big amenities or a super quiet retreat.

text.text:
Very poor experience here.

We arrived expecting a straightforward check in after travelling over 10 hours from the UK with our baby. What followed was one of the most stressful hotel experiences we have had.

There were no staff on site when we arrived. Guests are directed to pay at a self service machine next to a restaurant where your room key is activated.

When we reached our room, we realised there was no cot despite having requested one in advance as we were travelling with an infant.

I went back downstairs and found a sign stating that there are no staff on site after 12pm and that guests must contact a WhatsApp number if assistance is required.

After waiting for a reply, we were told via WhatsApp that nobody was available to help until the following day. There was no attempt to resolve the situation.

All communication was via WhatsApp and the language and tone of the messages were extremely poor. The responses were badly written, informal and did not read like communication from a professionally run hotel.

“Sorry about that , contact you three party and request de refund”

At a time when we needed urgent help, it felt unreliable and deeply concerning.

There was no manager, no night staff and no one physically present who could assist. We were left messaging someone remotely who could not offer any practical solution.

With no safe sleeping arrangement for our baby, staying was not an option. Late in the evening, we had to find and book alternative accommodation.

At the time, we were told that a note would be sent to management to arrange a refund. We felt reassured that although chaotic, the situation would at least be handled fairly.

After ignoring follow up messages and emails for a six days, the hotel finally came back (again via WhatsApp) and refused to refund us. Despite informing them within an hour of check in that we had been forced to leave, they now claim the room was technically available for the duration of the stay and that a cot is not guaranteed, despite advertising free cots available on request.

The combination of no on site staff, remote only messaging and unprofessional communication left us feeling extremely uncomfortable and unsupported.

We would strongly caution others before booking. Try the Plymouth hotel instead - they were great and it actually feels like a boutique hotel.

I have stayed here twice before, and while it wasn’t great, it was tolerable. After this most recent stay, however, I will never return. This was the worst hotel experience I have ever had.

We reserved a king room but were assigned room 311, which had two full beds instead. When I spoke to the front desk, I was told the only other available room had a moldy smell and that there were no other rooms to switch to.

In room 311, the air conditioning was “master controlled,” and we were unable to lower it below 74 degrees. We asked the front desk for help, and the employee truly did everything she could. She even showed us that her system would not allow the temperature to be set any lower. By morning, the room was 81 degrees and extremely humid. I honestly would have rather slept outside. I have never stayed at a hotel where you can’t control the temp yourself...it’s completely unacceptable.

The bed sheets didn’t fit properly, and every time you sat down, one corner would come loose. The carpets were also extremely dirty, so we wore shoes the entire time.

I want to emphasize that the front desk employee was very helpful, apologetic, and did her best to resolve the issues. It’s clear this is not a staff problem, but a result of ownership failing to properly maintain and manage the property.

text.text:
Fairwind Hotel Miami (1000 Collins Ave) | Clean and well-located, but fee transparency and basic functionality need work.

I stayed one night on Feb 6 (pre-cruise) and the biggest positives were the location and cleanliness. The hotel is in the heart of South Beach to walkable restaurants and about a block from the beach. My room was immaculately clean, and the 20% discount at the on-site restaurants with your room key was a nice perk.

That said, the experience was held back by several issues. At check-in, you pay a $35 resort fee that I did not see disclosed when booking, along with a $100 incidental hold. Also, the payment kiosks were down, and the manager said he had to manually enter my card, which created unnecessary concern.

The room (212) was much smaller than the online photos suggested and lacked basic functionality: no chair and no desk. The bathroom setup was awkward: the vent was positioned over the toilet rather than the shower, towel racks were placed over/near the toilet instead of by the shower (so you have to step out and walk to retrieve towels), and there were no power outlets in the bathroom, so shaving/grooming had to be done by the bed. The sink also drained very slowly. I reported it and was told someone would come up, but no one ever did. Bathroom lack shelving or counter top space.

Overall, it served its purpose for a quick overnight before heading to PortMiami, but the surprise fees, room mismatch, and lack of follow-through on service make it hard to rate higher.

text.text:
Checked into the room at 7pm and found the bedding wet!  Had to text their virtual front desk to inform them as this property doesn’t have any onsite staff.  We were sent a code to a storage room where bedding was supposed to be - but nothing in there but towels.
We stripped the bed and now noticed that the bed was wet from the sheets and the room smelt musky.  Texted them again and requested a new room but were told they didn’t have any available.  It’s clear that the cleaning staff put wet sheets on the bed.  With nobody returning our calls and only communicating through text we decided to leave this hotel and go to a different one across the street.
Mistakes happen but it is how this hotel is handling the aftermath that should scare you away.  The employee named Niccolo was rude and intimidating and would only agree to refund our stay if we didn’t write a bad review.  I told him the refund should not be contingent on my review. They refused to refund our stay and hung up on me.  This is not the way to handle a situation. I would never recommend this hotel.

Also:
Difficulty getting access codes on check in
Toilet paper stuffed in door peeophole
No glassware
No way to prevent the door from being opened from the outside
NO staff whatsoever - pray nothing goes wrong!

text.text: 3.5/5 stars. The best thing about the hotel is its location. 2 minutes from the beach, many cafes and restaurants, grocery stores, clubs, etc. With that, it was quite noisy at night - you can clearly hear all of the street traffic. Not sure about other rooms, but ours had a window that was taped shut so we couldn’t open it. Probably wouldn’t have wanted to anyway since the view was an alleyway. The room itself is outdated and the bathroom could use an upgrade, but overall it was pretty comfortable and had what we needed. The second best thing is the reception staff and service. They are so kind, attentive, and helpful if you have any questions or requests. I would stay here again, but with ear plugs!

text.text:
**WORTH READING***
This has been one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had. When I arrived, the room looked dirty, and aside from the bed being made, it clearly wasn’t properly cleaned. On top of that, the night manager mistakenly charged my card over $400 for parking, despite the fact that I was already paying $370+ for the room. He claimed he immediately refunded the money, but when I checked out, I was told no refund had actually been processed until the GM handled it later.

I spent almost two weeks going back and forth with the staff. First, they refunded just $30, then told me they would only return $336 because of that initial refund—forcing me to send receipts, screenshots, and proof that they were consistently giving me wrong information. In the end, they still never refunded the full amount, and I had to go through my bank to get my money back, which took another 30 days.

Now, four months later, the hotel randomly charged my account $375 again—even though I’m nowhere near Miami and have not stayed there since. This is completely unacceptable. Not only do they make repeated billing errors, but they also offer no compensation, no apology, and no sense of responsibility for the stress and inconvenience they cause. They act as if simply issuing refunds—months later—is good enough.

This hotel should honestly be taken over by a company that knows how to run a property correctly and maintain proper billing practices. No one should have to deal with money being taken out of their account at random, especially during the holiday season.

I don't care for hotels that surprise me upon checkin with a freaking "resort fee."  That's a shady way of doing business.  You can't tell me up front when I book and pay for the room???  There's another fee I have to pay in order to get into the room when I arrive???    A resort fee?
And, I'm told there's a resort fee because "the room is equipped with 2 bottles of water and I can use a beach chair."   $33.  I'm only here 12 hours.  When a guest is only here 12 hours the "resort fee" should be waived.
Plus, this place that charges a "resort fee"...does not serve breakfast.
How do you call yourself a "resort"....when you don't serve breakfast.  Roadside motels in rural America serve a continental breakfast, but this "resort" doesn't??   I gotta walk next door to the Holiday Inn (where I will be staying next time)??

Room was nice but had bugs.  One in the sink and one on the wall.

text.text:
We had a very nice stay here but there were a few things worth noting that we did not like.
The hotel is currently undergoing renovations, starting with the penthouse floor and we were right below that so we heard quite a bit of the construction. The service elevator was clearly not working since the construction workers were using the guest elevators, of which there were only 2. This made for long wait times for the elevators.
Our room was ready for us immediately upon check in (earlier than normal check in time), which was amazing! And while it was spotlessly clean and had a stunning ocean view, there were noticeable holes in the curtains and shower curtain. There were many signs of wear/tear all over the hotel, making it clear why the renovation was needed.
The pool was NOT heated and this made a huge difference. Despite the 80 degree weather and warm (strong) winds, the water was too cold for me to go in and my kids even took a long time getting used to the water.
The beach staff were very nice and even came over to where the kids were digging in the sand to place an umbrella over them. There were also sand toys for them to play with.
The staff were exceptional. Front desk people were friendly, the cafe staff were amazing, and housekeeping did an amazing job keeping our room clean.
Would recommend this hotel for anyone on a budget.

text.text:
Extremely disappointing stay.

Check-in set the tone: the front desk didn’t greet me at all—when I walked up, the employee just said “ID.” No welcome, no smile. I also booked a standard room with one bed but was going to be put in a room with two small beds instead. I’m a Platinum Elite member and received no acknowledgment of status and no welcome gift.

The room itself was unacceptable. There was toilet paper with pubic hair on it in the toilet, hair on the towels, and what looked like blood or nail polish on the bathtub. The room phone’s service buttons didn’t work at all.  The key cards repeatedly failed—they had to be reprogrammed at check-in and then again the next day because they stopped working before checkout.  The view was of rooftop mechanical equipment that made constant noise day and night.

The property is also poorly maintained. Peeling paint, a peeling office chair in the room, and in the fitness room, the treadmill belt seam was separating, which is honestly a huge safety hazard.

Between the rude service, cleanliness issues, and maintenance problems, this stay fell far below what I expect from a Holiday Inn. Management should seriously address these issues.

text.text: Did a quick weekend getaway for a friend’s birthday. We picked this hotel because of the location of the beach which was the only good thing. When we first arrived the gentleman at the desk seemed friendly until he told me how there is a $25 a day fee for the hotel (which was fine) I said I didn’t know that he told me I didn’t read the fine print. Then after checking in our room we had no towels or toilet paper and the AC wasn’t working in the room. I also paid for 2 queen size beds and the beds in the room were full size and also the shower was in the middle of the room which was not shown on Expedia site for this hotel. I went back down to the front desk and Terry told me I get what I paid for and that all the hotels in the area were double in price. Not the best customer service. Worst Hotel Experience in Miami – Never Again
This was hands down the worst hotel stay I’ve ever had in Miami. Absolutely unacceptable from start to finish.
First, they charged a cleaning fee for four days, yet housekeeping showed up only once. What exactly was I paying for? Definitely not cleanliness or service.
Any time I asked for help, no service was provided. When I requested fresh towels, I was flat-out told they had none. How does a hotel not have towels?
Breakfast was a complete joke — just coffee and boiled eggs. That’s it. No options, no effort. I literally said “WTH?” out loud.
The front desk staff were rude and arrogant. When my key card stopped working (which happens all the time in hotels), instead of fixing it professionally, they said, “We can’t keep doing this,” as if it was somehow my fault. Zero customer service, zero accountability.
This place does not deserve to call itself a hotel. Poor service, hidden fees, rude staff, and no basic amenities.
Worst Miami stay experience ever.
I will never come back and strongly suggest others avoid this place too.

text.text:
This review is for anyone who is vacationing here with the intentions of driving - meaning you rented a car and plan to travel by driving yourself.

I do not recommend this place as a place to do so. In fact - if you are driving I don’t recommend staying in Miami period.

It’s incredibly not-driver-friendly. The parking spots here are incredibly limited and extremely hard to park into. Unless you are renting a truck or a high-clearance vehicle, you will struggle. The way the parking spaces are located you will have to jump the curb. No way around that.

We stayed in room 208. The toilet does not flush. There was an unlined rubbish bin that we used to fill up with water to manually flush the toilets. The shower had little pressure. Anyone with long or lots of hair will find themselves showering for a long time.

If you are on foot however and you don’t mind the subpar room amenities - I actually think this place isn’t that bad. Just remember you will need to depend on either ride shares or the public transportation to get to anywhere.

I do wish that the property management company invest in upgrading their room card readers. The cards they use are extremely out of date and are extremely sensitive to data corruption. The receptionist who checked us in kept repeating herself to emphasize that the card cannot be near smart phones or wallet. Anything NFC or RFID capable will corrupt the card and you will be locked out of your room. Happened to us and other residents.

They do however have 24/7 front desk service so I guess it’s not that bad.

I accidentally booked two weeks later than intended and immediately called the third party agent to ask for the 7 nights booking to be cancelled and I would rebook the correct dates (the online reservation calendar jumps to a date 2 weeks forward and highlights that day which misleads a distracted mind). They contacted the hotel who refused the request and would not transfer or allow a refund of any amount for cancellation. I decided to book another night and headed to the hotel to check in and try to negotiate a fair outcome. The receptionist reiterated the hotel policy which of course is not fair or necessary just because you have written acquisitive terms and greedy conditions into a policy.  So we stayed the night and turned out we would have abandoned our reservation anyway given the disgusting state of the property. The room and furnishings were filthy and of very poor quality. The walls are paper thin and the property sits on a main road so you are disturbed by noise from inside and outside the building. The ceiling fan was misaligned and also making lots of noise so had to be turned off. We dressed in track suits to minimize contact with the bed sheets which smelled like body odor and triggered formication or possibly we were actually being bitten by bed bugs. The WIFI is so slow as to be unusable and the staff were combative when we requested it be remedied.
It really is a two star hotel at best and the 2.5 stars they had needs to be amended.

text.text:
If you’re looking for a sophisticated yet approachable escape in the heart of Mid-Beach, Le Particulier Miami is a hidden gem that absolutely nails the "modern Miami" aesthetic. I recently stopped by to try their cafe, and the experience was top-tier from the moment I walked through the door.
Modern Design Meets Art Deco Soul
The first thing you notice is the atmosphere. The design is very nice and modern, successfully blending 1980s glamour with a minimalist Art Deco twist. The space feels incredibly chic, with a palette of soft pastels, warm oak, and brass accents that make it feel more like a private sanctuary than a standard hotel lobby. It’s the kind of place where you actually want to linger and soak in the "lobby oasis" vibe rather than just grabbing your drink and rushing out.
The Perfect Americano
I’m quite particular about my coffee, but the Americano here was great. It was well-balanced, smooth, and served at the perfect temperature—not bitter at all, which is a common pitfall. Whether you’re a local needing a quiet place to work for an hour or a traveler looking for a high-quality caffeine fix, their cafe service is efficient and the quality is undeniable.
Final Thoughts
The location on Collins Avenue is ideal—tucked away from the chaotic noise of South Beach but still vibrant and accessible. The staff were friendly and unhurried, which really adds to the "lifestyle" feel of the property. Between the stunning interior design and the excellent coffee, it’s a spot I’ll definitely be returning to. It’s a perfect example of how a modern boutique hotel should handle its food and beverage experience.

text.text:
Positives:  Big open room. Large refrigerator with ice maker (water dispenser broken unfortunately).  Front desk answers the phone most of the time (but they do not call you back if you leave a message).  They went from 2 to 3 stars for printing our cruise luggage tags for us.

Negatives: lots of single paned windows with cheap 1” miniblinds that do not block light or dampen sound. Curtains really aren’t that expensive and if you got thick curtains, it would block out the ridiculous amount of honking and noise. It would also keep me from being awakened in an incredibly bright room as soon as the sun comes up.  This may not be as problematic on rear facing rooms, but we were third floor facing street, Very loud.

Don’t believe that you’ll be able to watch TV in the room. I know you don’t come to Miami to watch TV, but at some point it’s nice to be able to turn on the TV and wind down, or in my case I wanted some background noise to block out the ridiculous outside noise . They should fire DIRECTV and get with the new times. The Wi-Fi is decent after I asked them to reset the modem because it wasn’t working very well. Network TV and streaming would fix a lot of problems, but the satellite pixelates every five seconds.  The worker came up and just said what’s the problem, that is what satellite does. Um, no, not on a clear night.

Please put some coffee in the room when there is a coffee maker already there. It’s not expensive and it’s a great luxury after a terrible night of sleep.

For me ultimately the value of a hotel is ability to relax and get a good night sleep.  We were planning to come back after the cruise, but they failed at this, so I cancelled the room for next week.

text.text: We stayed here with 2 adult kids and our 5 year old grandson for 5 nights because the hotel is located not far from relatives.  Although the suite was clean and had plenty of space we found the hotel to be inhospitable and the front desk to be unfriendly.  Although we had booked for 5 people when we arrived only 2 beds were made up and there were insufficient sheets and towels and when we asked for more  we were told they would be sent up but that did not happen until we went back again hours later.  When a pipe burst in our room the staff did come up to stop the leak and mop the room as soon as we called them, and they did quickly offer a replacement room but left us to drag our own bags and possessions through the floodwater and upstairs to the new room without offering to assist as our grandson cried. And then we once again had to pull out and make 3 of the beds in the new room- no assistance from hotel staff.  This ruined what was meant to be a relaxing afternoon but when we asked for a courtesy discount or accommodation at checkout the person at the front desk who identified himself as the owner declined and seemed to think the hotel should get an award for supplying a replacement room.  Personally I think we are fortunate they had a replacement room available because the feeling we were left with is that if they did not they would have just told us to checkout or offered us to stay in the flooded room without any discount. On Friday night when we returned to the hotel from dinner we were met by a panicked non-English speaking hotel guest who identified himself to us in Yiddish and Hebrew as a fellow Sabbath observer who was locked out of his room and asked us for help communicating the issue with the front desk. The attendant at the front desk indicated he knew the man was a hotel guest and was amenable to providing the gentleman with a new keycard but refused to cooperate at all to open his door for him. I assisted the man in communicating with another friendly hotel guest who genially agreed to come up and open his room door. While I do not expect Sabbath accommodation from every hotel we stay in (and we in fact left our door open to avoid bothering them), I do feel that in the circumstances where a guest of the hotel needed the simple courtesy of assistance in opening his door a decent and hospitable hotel would spend the 3 minutes to assist him as we have found to be the case in numerous other hotels both nationally and internationally. But in this case the desk attendant informed us that is was “not his problem” and suggested that this man find another guest to assist him (which as mentioned we were able to do because unlike the hotel attendant, the other guests wanted to be helpful). In any event if you are looking for hospitality in Miami Beach there are plenty of other hotels, and I’d recommend finding a different one.

text.text:
I ended my membership after many years because the overall experience has become unacceptable.

Service quality is consistently poor. Staff members often appear unmotivated, insufficiently trained, and in some cases openly unfriendly. Simple requests turn into drawn-out processes, food service takes an unreasonable amount of time, and the end result rarely justifies the wait.

The beach area is almost permanently overcrowded and poorly managed. Instead of feeling exclusive or relaxing, it feels hectic and neglected. Several areas of the property are visibly worn down, poorly maintained, and at times simply unpleasant to use. This is not an environment where you feel comfortable spending time.

What ultimately led to my decision was the general lack of respect shown toward members. Rules are enforced in an unnecessarily confrontational way, without empathy or basic judgment. Rather than feeling welcomed, you are made to feel like a problem.

Avoid becoming a member.

When you call to request that your room is clean you’re typically on hold for 10 to 20 minutes. I assume they do this in order to dissuade you from getting your room cleaned so that they don’t have to pay housekeepers.

Meanwhile, I have tipped every day for every housekeeper.

BUYER BEWARE.

text.text:
I'm writing this review as a warning to those who are considering renting a suite at the Residences via Airbnb and NOT through the hotel.  The Private Residences management company based in NYC that manages units in this building via Airbnb essentially STOLE $2,807.54 from me.  I'm shocked and alarmed at how little protection the paying customer has in the arrangement.   Airbnb is essentially indifferent to the theft.  And Fontainebleau management themselves has very little authority in the situation.

Had I known we had so little protection as a paying customer I never would have gone through Airbnb.

My wife and her girlfriends rented a two bedroom suite for 3 nights at the Residences via airbnb for a weekend getaway.  It was our first time using the service and it seemed like a good deal.  On Friday October 11th they checked into the room and found it to be dirty and in disrepair.  Attached are photos.  The deal-breaker issues were mold on the fridge and shower (one guest had allergies) and the poorly patched fist-sized holes in the walls (another guest was a survivor of domestic violence) There were also stains on the curtains, splatters on the walls around the toilet, scattered sticky spots, hair and clothing tags on the floor, etc.  Very grimy vibe.  They felt extremely uncomfortable and immediately notified airbnb and the front desk at the hotel.  The Host did offer another room to stay in, but they were exhausted & disheartened with the airbnb experience so they opted to cancel the room and purchase 2 new rooms directly from the Fontainebleau hotel.  And then things got sketchy.

The Host refused to check them out of the suite or let them cancel the reservation, and then went dark. The next day, the Host texted novels of excuses and accusations, how unreasonable they were being for not wanting to stay in the Suite.  The case was escalated within airbnb, but the Host was unresponsive.  Finally on Sunday my wife sat down with a manager at Fontainebleau owner services who was very kind, and she checked them out of the suite.  The manager said there was nothing else the Hotel could do,  but we did get a printout from housekeeping documenting that the room was never used.

When the trip ended on Monday, October 14th we followed up on the case with airbnb and were told that.......
1. You can't get a full refund because you never checked out of the room.
2. The Host doesn't have to check you out early if they don't want to, even if you ask them to do it.  The Host also doesn't have to answer you if they don't feel like it.
3. The maximum refund you can get is 10% for the cleaning fee and a $300 courtesy credit.
4. It's at the Host's discretion if you get a refund or not.  If the Host says no, Airbnb is powerless to do anything.  Airbnb takes no responsibility and won't cover your loses.
5.  Even though airbnb acknowledges the room was dirty and in disrepair, it wasn't dirty ENOUGH to qualify for any further action.

The first airbnb rep I spoke with issued an ultimatum, that if I didn't take the partial credit by the end of her shift she was logging out of her terminal and closing our case, and I would get nothing.

Finally after 3 weeks of back-and-forth with airbnb we were able to get a little under $1,000 back, but still lost over $1,800 for a suite no-one stayed in.  I've never had so much taken from me in exchange for nothing.   Please think twice before using airbnb (or any 3rd party site for that matter) when booking your vacation.  You have no protection as a consumer.  And if you don't like what you're being given they will just keep your money anyway.

I scoured their policy online, and that is not listed. They said it was an internal policy.  Even if it was a policy, these policies are illegal based on Florida law. I'm disputing this with my credit card now, and will file small claims, but I would avoid this Roami company. What a mistake not going with a reputable company. Learned my lesson.

text.text:
We stayed here for four nights and wish we stayed elsewhere.

Pros
- Convenient beach access
- Rooms were stylish and we had good experiences with housekeeping

Cons
- Service was sub par for a five star hotel. The front desk and breakfast at the hotel at aguasal in particular. Upon checkin the front desk was ill informed of the pool/beach closure for the event and told us the beach was open to the public. Turns out only one of the pools was closed, but a shocking first encounter for a reported five star hotel.
At breakfast we were forgotten by a server on multiple occasions and waited 30 minutes to get our coffee. The hostess also struggled with crowd control and there is often a line for breakfast.
- pools were extremely overcrowded, they shouldn’t be closing one of the pools for an event when majority of guests are not affiliated with the event.
- service at the beach can be very slow and if you miss the waiter it could be an hour until you see them again.
- the rooms are very loud, we had to hook our phones up to the Bluetooth to play white noise.
- this is not a kid friendly hotel, their website even says it’s best for couples and solo travelers. That said, there are hoards of misbehaved children. If you are looking for a romantic, adult focused resort, look else where.

text.text:
My stay at **Andaz Miami Beach** was nothing short of exceptional — a true 5-star property delivering a 5-star experience from start to finish.

I arrived looking for refuge from a snowstorm, and the property manager could not have been more gracious. He kindly upgraded my room, which was such a thoughtful gesture, and even sent a personal note along with a delicious treat waiting for me. That level of care and attention immediately made me feel welcomed and valued.

The room was absolutely beautiful — elegant, comfortable, and immaculately maintained. The pools were stunning and perfectly heated, making it easy to relax and unwind. While there are no hot tubs (which makes sense for Florida’s climate), one would certainly be a nice addition during the cooler winter months. The beach experience was just as lovely, and having two chairs and umbrellas included in the resort fee made it effortless to enjoy the oceanfront setting.

Although I didn’t have the opportunity to dine at the main restaurant, the poolside restaurant was delicious. We tried the burgers, salad, and salmon — all fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. It was the perfect complement to a relaxing day by the pool.

Another major plus: when paying fully with points, there were no additional fees — a rare and much-appreciated benefit that adds incredible value.

From the warm, personalized service to the beautiful accommodations and amenities, everything exceeded expectations. I would absolutely return — a flawless escape when I needed it most. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

text.text:
We booked a room at the Hotel Continental because of its proximity to the beach and its affordability compared to most of the Hilton properties south of 40th Street in Miami Beach.  We knew what we were in for in terms of amenities and room size, but were not at all disappointed.  The room was clean and the king mattress was great and we slept better here than in any Hampton Inn, HGI, etc which have huge welts in their mattresses.  Even the AC was smooth and calming.  It never woke us.

Leo checked us in and was very personable during our stay.  He had a great attitude about him.  Katy was very sweet and conversational with my wife and me.  She served us during happy hours and the next mornings at breakfast.  We loved talking with her and appreciated her hustle.

We used the hotel-provided, free beach chairs and towels each day and parked them close to the water’s edge, in front of the encampments from the neighboring Cadillac and Andaz hotels.  Our needs were simple this vacation, but the Hotel Continental managed to exceed our expectations.

text.text:
We stayed in the Sorrento Tower, and while the view and location are nice, the actual experience was extremely disappointing for the price.

The room felt worn out and poorly maintained. Lighting was dim, the space did not feel properly cleaned, and the furniture on the deck was damaged, with broken and neglected items left outside. The overall condition of the room did not match what you would expect at this price point.

Basic amenities were a problem throughout the stay. The fridge in our room did not work, and food stored inside went warm. The bathtub would not drain, and the jets turned on randomly in the middle of the night, which was unsettling. The in-room washer and dryer were unusable due to a cut power cord, something we only discovered on the last night after loading it with laundry. Front desk staff had even sent detergent earlier, so there was no indication the machine didn’t work.

For a supposedly premium room, the coffee maker was the same basic Keurig you’d find in a low-end two-star hotel, which summed up the overall lack of attention to quality.

Check-in was also a mess. We were not given the correct rooms initially, and it took over half an hour to get things sorted out. On top of that, staff were consistently rude and difficult to get clear information from, which made the entire stay more frustrating than it needed to be.

Sorrento Tower is significantly overpriced for the condition and level of service provided. There are much better options in the area for less money. We would not stay in Sorrento Tower again and would not recommend it.

Staying at Sorrento Tower in Fontainebleau Hotel, which I booked via Mak Property, was an absolute dream come true.
From the moment we stepped into our suite, we were greeted with breathtaking views of both Miami Beach and the downtown skyline – a sight that left us in awe every single day.
The sunsets from our suite were nothing short of magical, golden glow over the cityscape, creating an unforgettable backdrop for our evenings.
Speaking of the suite, it was impeccably designed and furnished with every comfort in mind. From the luxurious bedding to the spacious living area and fully-equipped, it truly felt like a home away from home.
The fact that it was serviced only added to the convenience and relaxation of our stay.

One of the highlights of our experience was the seamless access to all the amenities of the hotel and the beach. Whether we wanted to lounge by the pool, indulge in a spa treatment, or simply soak up the sun on the pristine sands of Miami Beach, everything was just steps away.
But perhaps what made our stay truly exceptional was the vibrant atmosphere that permeated every corner of the property. From the lively poolside scene to the buzzing energy of the beach club, there was never a dull moment during our stay.
Our stay at Sorrento Tower exceeded all expectations and left us with memories that will last a lifetime. We can't wait to return for another unforgettable experience in the heart of Miami Beach.

text.text:
We were initially very happy with our stay—the apartment was clean, well-furnished, and offered a stunning view. The check-in process was smooth, and the host communicated promptly and clearly. These were the highlights of our experience.

However, what ultimately ruined our trip and left us deeply disappointed was the building’s elevator situation, which was not disclosed by the host in any way prior to our booking. The elevators were barely functioning throughout our stay. We often had to wait 40–70 minutes just to catch one, and on several occasions, we had no choice but to take the stairs—even from the 34th floor.

The most alarming incident involved my 13-year-old son, who got trapped in an elevator on the 23rd floor along with four other people. There were no working emergency alarms and no phone signal. They remained stuck until the doors eventually opened on their own. My son was terrified and ran down the stairs in a panic.

My husband, who is elderly and has mobility limitations, was effectively stuck in the apartment for most of our stay because he simply could not use the stairs. This situation caused enormous stress, physical strain, and completely disrupted the plans we had for our trip.

To make things worse, we learned from others in the building that this elevator issue is long-standing and well known—yet the host never mentioned it in the listing or during our communications. We felt misled and uninformed about a major safety and accessibility concern. Even after reporting the issue early during our stay, no meaningful action or compensation was offered.

At checkout, we had to begin the process hours early, anticipating long elevator delays, and struggled to move our luggage and help my husband exit safely.

While the apartment itself has potential, the ongoing elevator crisis and lack of transparency from the host made this a deeply stressful and disappointing experience. I would strongly advise future guests to ask direct questions about the elevator functionality before booking, especially if traveling with elderly family members or young children.

We had a wonderful stay at the Courtyard by Marriott Downtown Miami, and the customer service truly made the experience stand out. I especially want to recognize Sebastian at the front desk, who went above and beyond for our family.

Our plans changed at the last minute when our two boys unexpectedly joined the trip, and Sebastian was incredibly accommodating with a short-term upgrade request. He handled everything with professionalism, warmth, and genuine care, making what could have been a stressful situation completely seamless.

Throughout our stay, he consistently checked in to make sure our needs were met and took the time to provide thoughtful recommendations around Miami, which we really appreciated. It’s moments like these that remind you of the true value of being a Marriott Bonvoy member—feeling recognized, valued, and treated with special care.

Thank you to Sebastian and the entire team for making our stay so enjoyable. We will absolutely be back and highly recommend this hotel to others.

I've stayed at many Marriott hotels over the years, and this was by far the worst experience I've ever had. We stayed from Thursday to Monday at a rate of $600 per night, which sets a certain expectation for quality and service unfortunately, this property did not meet those expectations at all.

In addition to the room rate, we were charged $75 per day for parking and a $35 daily destination fee, yet there were no meaningful amenities or services that justified those added costs. To make matters worse, one of our family vehicles was damaged while in the hotel's possession, which was extremely upsetting and added unnecessary stress to our stay.

The customer service was extremely disappointing. Staff were unhelpful and unresponsive, and there was no sense of hospitality or support throughout our visit.

The breakfast was another major letdown - $57 for food that was cold and of very poor quality. Overall, this hotel does not reflect a five-star experience in any way.

Very disappointing stay. We will not be returning.

text.text:
I am currently staying at this hotel and it is 1:30 a.m. as I write this review. I chose this property because it is advertised as a 5-star hotel, has an overall rating of 4.4, and is close to the cruise port.
When booking, I explained that we would have four people. The representative recommended a one-bedroom suite and assured me it would include two double beds, a pull-out couch, and a rollaway bed. However, the room we were given had only one king bed.
At check-in, we requested that the pull-out couch be set up and that a rollaway bed be brought to the room. We left for dinner expecting everything to be ready when we returned so we could rest after a long day of travel. When we came back, nothing had been done. We called the front desk and were told someone would be sent up. After waiting over 30 minutes, we ended up going to the front desk in person. Someone finally came up and set up the couch bed, but there was still no rollaway.
After both of our children showered, we were still missing the rollaway. My husband went back to the front desk and was then told that rollaway beds are not permitted in this room because of the carpet—completely contradicting everything we had been told previously. At that point, we were expected to have our 12-year-old daughter and 14-year-old son share a couch bed.
I went downstairs again, and thankfully, a very kind manager was able to get us a rollaway bed. I truly appreciate her effort and willingness to help when no one else would.
Additionally, the room was only stocked with two sets of towels for four people. It took a very long time—and multiple requests—before additional towels were delivered.
The room itself is disappointing. The carpet does not appear to have been vacuumed, and there is visible black mold around the edges of the shower, which is extremely unpleasant. At this point, I am still trying to figure out how I am going to sleep here. Both of my children are still awake, and even they feel like they are “roughing it.”
If you value a clean hotel room, I do not recommend staying here. If you expect timely service for simple requests like towels or bedding, I also do not recommend this hotel. This stay has been a huge disappointment, and it is not how we wanted to start our cruise, especially after such a long travel day.
I do want to acknowledge the very kind young woman at the front desk who ultimately helped us with the rollaway bed. She genuinely tried her best, and I am thankful for her assistance.
I have pictures of the black mold in the shower and even in the sink where you brush your teeth if I could figure out how to add it to this review from my phone, I will.

It shares a building with the Marriott and is supposed to feel more personal, though the only real touch was a glass of champagne at check‑in. The pool was closed, and we were directed to use the Kimpton’s pool next door—which was actually much nicer. Amenities were limited, there was no fridge, and valet parking was the only option at $75 a night, yet it consistently took over 20 minutes to retrieve the car. The gym was the only standout feature. I wouldn’t stay again—there are much better options in the area

I think you should let some moths pass by and then they can finish full remodeling in order to make a pleasant stay for you.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ An Exceptional Miami Stay at YVE Hotel

My recent stay at YVE Hotel Miami was nothing short of wonderful.

From the moment I arrived, the team were warm, welcoming and effortlessly professional — the kind of hospitality that truly makes one feel at home. The atmosphere is vibrant yet relaxed, perfectly capturing the energy of downtown Miami while still offering comfort and calm.

It may seem a small gesture, but it makes an enormous difference to a guest’s experience — and it was handled with such ease and charm.

Hospitality is about how you make people feel, and the team at YVE Hotel absolutely understand that.

I would happily return and highly recommend it to anyone visiting Miami.

Warmest thanks to the entire team.

Grant Harrold
The Royal Butler

We chose this hotel to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary because of its prime location. Overall, it wasn't disappointing, just mediocre, especially for me as a Platinum Elite member and longtime customer of IHG.

On the morning of our arrival, while we were at the airport, I received a call suggesting a downgrade from our one-bedroom suite to a standard room. I refused, and wasn't downgraded, but it left a bad taste.
Check-in went smoothly, no issues. The room was nice, but surprisingly noisy from the terrace and street below, even with the windows closed. The building's construction doesn't help. You can hear people walking on the floor above and in the hallway.  Rooms and windows are not soundproofed.
Housekeeping missed some spots on the floor during the cleaning. Bedding was basic, and the TV lacked streaming services or premium channels. For over $ 1,000 a night, there was no luxury feeling at all.
We requested a late checkout and were initially offered 12:30. After a bit of negotiation, it became 1:00, though it was implied my status isn't high enough for more. We understand it depends on availability, but it made us feel somewhat unwelcome.
On the positive side, the excellent location and great breakfast were the highlights.

text.text:
I booked a Solo trip to Miami for 4 nights at this hotel. I thought the location was great, and from the pictures I decided to book the "Bayview penthouse". I wanted to relax with beautiful views, room service, and a cozy "penthouse". I use quotations because the pictures did not reflect the room at all. I was totally catfished. First off, the staff was very nice and helpful, so no complaints there.
But the room looked nothing like the pictures. How can a room go from being humid and hot to humid and freezing?! I had to request an extra blanket, because even 1 degree changes the temperature to unbearably hot to unbearably cold, and I'd rather have it cold. The constant humidity in the room made me feel dirty the entire stay. Speaking of dirty, thank god I brought my own hygiene products because there was no hand soap, and the bodywash was completely empty in the "if a toilet on any floor flushes the water pressure and temperature will drop tremendously" shower. There were also no bath cloths, and the shower head was corroded and uneven.  The penthouse(s) are on the 17th floor of the hotel, and with only 2 slow elevators and the constant cruisers, I ended up using the stairs way more than I wanted. Just to run down to grab my delivery food was an entire 30 minute ordeal. The wi-fi didn't reach that far up, so I had access to about 10 channels on cable, no wi-fi or streaming services even pretended to be provided. My last night the TV just stopped working completely. There is no "room service", everything online was a complete facade.
The restaurant/bar at the hotel was pretty good but pricey, and they were weirdly out of ingredients to make their specialty cocktails my entire stay.
Sure, I'd recommend this place for anyone staying 1 night, but keep your expectations very low. The ownership sucks money out of your pocket without providing even a quarter of the quality they pretend to provide online. Do not stay here. What a waste of money. I'm giving 1 star because the staff was very nice.
