text.text: Classic bait and switch. Booked a room with a view and King bed. After checking and heading up to our room we walked into a  room with 2 doubles. I'm a pretty big guy that likes to sleep in the same bed as his wife which is why we picked a King bed. Headed back down to the front desk to see if they could resolve the issue and was told no Kings were available. Nevermind that we  reserved and paid extra for a King. When I mentioned about needing the extra room the guy behind the desk said 2 doubles are as much room as a king. After calling BS on that remark he said let me get my manager. The manager arrives and looks at our email reservation that states king, looks at his system and says it's our email that is wrong and not an error on his end and if we didn't want to stay in the room he would cancel the reservation. At this point is was about the fact they didn't take any accountability, never offered an apology or discount on the room that we paid extra for, just a "take it or leave it" attitude. No wonder they have a 3.5 star review which is about 3 stars higher then what they should have. Just try and make an effort to make your guests happy and reimburse them when mistakes are made. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend? Not a chance.

text.text: Overall, this hotel lives up to its 4-star reputation. It is a solid but unremarkable property. The entryway is quite underwhelming and the lobby, while on brand for Miami, looks better in pictures than in person. The carpets are stained and the overall vibe is neither tasteful nor elevated, but tacky. It looks like something an Instagrammer would appreciate. The food served at the on-site restaurant was mediocre. We stayed in the Executive Suite (the front desk was kind enough to upgrade us to one on a high floor, which is very much appreciated), and it was fine. The floor plan is U-shaped and the sitting area is far from the bedroom; it doesn't make the room feel particularly spacious. However, there are plenty of windows and you get a nice panoramic view. Our room, though being on a high floor, was overlooking the commuter railroad and the periodic noise pollution will definitely be an issue if you're a light sleeper. Calling the front desk takes numerous button presses and a longer-than-expected wait time. Overall, it is a good property, but if you're looking for a true luxury hotel in Brickell, you'll need to look down the road at Hotel AKA or JW Marriott, etc.

It really should be disclosed by the server or bartender.

text.text:
Conveniently located just a short walk away from the bustling Brickell city centre, this hotel is nothing short of amazing. There were many bicycles for rent to explore the area. There's a nearby park perfect for a morning walk. Novotel is located at a quiet residential area. Walgreens is just across the road. The roads here were quiet and it's cyclist and joggers friendly.

Beautiful lobby with lots of natural light. The restaurant located at the lobby has limited seatings but they were always busy, which makes the place come alive.

The rooms were typical of rooms of a business hotel. Minimalist amenities. No room slippers, no toothbrush, no nothing as they are an eco friendly hotel, which is acceptable. The power sockets however, do not have international plugs. I enjoyed the TV programmes as there were many channels to select. Stayed there for 5 nights and I was recovering from my jetlag half the time.

Air-conditioning wasn't working at some point and someone from the engineering department was prompt to fix the issue upon informing the front office.

Shower space in the bathroom was decent with enough moving space and water does not splash out easily. The shower head however, had very sharp corners and I accidentally cut myself a few times when I bring it down to shower my toddler. (Room 914)

text.text: After reading the great reviews about Nuovo Properties, I was excited to confirm my booking for my first trip to Miami on 5/25/2018. But what I am about to share CAN NOT be made up! Firstly, the physical address to the property was not included in the initial email with their multiple paragraphs of “house rules” which led me to depend on google. Google sends me to the corporate office, instead of the actual location I’ll be sleeping at. But small matters, i decided to stay optimistic. But after finding the property and checking in, I was immediately disappointed, down, unhappy, and fed up by the company and their presentation for a few reasons. I was saddened by the lack of upkeep as the power was off in the bedroom. The two towels provided were folded nicely but filthy, and wreaked of filth and sweat. The white walls were filthy. The bathroom tiles were disgusting. There was dust everywhere, and the three beautiful lamps were without lightbulbs. I was also offended by the inability to take accountability after calling, texting, and emailing Nuovo Properties countless consecutive times with my concerns- to no avail! Lastly, the audacity of the company to not only ignore me and disregard my messages ALL weekend, but to keep nearly a thousand dollars of my money for three nights of this horrifying experience that caused me to buy new towels at the target on the corner of the property because the washing machine was broke, and cleaning supplies  is simply appalling. I would have been open to changing rooms, or even getting my money back in order to rent an actual hotel with working lights that would enable me to see after 8pm on my vacation- but Nuovo took my options away from me because they were unsung my entire experience. Potential customers, please learn from my poor experience and AVOID THIS PLACE! Regretfully, Christopher.God bless!

The angular, mirrored guest room aims for cool and quirky but lands on uncomfortable and awkward.  It's mainly a bed, with a hugely uncomfortable mattress and old pillows so uncomfortable that our necks hurt. No desk, no night tables, no convenient outlets, one little, hard chair. It's not a room for relaxing in. You have to inch your way around the bed to get to the bathroom or to the closet area with its broken drawers.

Same for the bathroom - with its 1" sink basin, and a sliding glass door that will either close the shower stall or give you privacy on the toilet. It looks kinda cool but so inefficient (Who designed that lol). Definitely not built with an older guest in mind.

The balcony was filthy, with an old crummy couch and a tiny table.

The pool area is nice but currently inundated by chunks of concrete from the nearby construction. A piece hit my husband. The lounge chairs are covered in concrete pieces.

Pluses:
- Outstanding housekeeping.
- Pleasant staff

I would not recommend staying here.
The room felt extremely confined, with no windows and very limited ventilation. Each door had a visible padlock, which created an unsettling, institutional atmosphere rather than a welcoming place to stay. It felt more like a holding space than a guest accommodation.
The bathroom was shared with other guests and filled with their personal belongings, which made it uncomfortable and lacked basic privacy.
The sleeping arrangement was a cot with a thin plastic mattress that made noise with every movement, making it nearly impossible to rest. Strong cooking smells from the shared area added to the discomfort.
The most concerning issue was that I briefly stepped outside and the entry code was changed, leaving me locked out without warning. As a paying guest, this was extremely stressful and unacceptable.
This experience did not meet reasonable standards of comfort, privacy, or communication.

The front desk was courteous. The lobby manager was cheerful and greeted us good morning. He even took our plates away after breakfast.
The only thing that seems lacking is a room safe to store your valuables when you are away.

At the hotel front desk, we booked a shuttle bus service to the terminal at $8 US per person. Seemed like a great option, however on the departure date, there were a dozen of people waiting for the shuttle bus (emphasize that this is a third party shuttle bus company and NOT operated by the hotel)
and the shuttle bus never came. The hotel personnel explained that the shuttle bus company did not receive the list before.......
Anyway, we ended up taking a taxi to the terminal.
Again, not the hotel fault but perhaps a different shuttle bus company can be engaged.

P.S. the taxi driver told us that on a busy day where there are lots of cruise ships on the terminal, it can take more than an hour to go there due to traffic and other drop off points.
A different perspective for you to consider.....

I do not recommend this hotel.
At check-in, we were informed that our reservation had supposedly been canceled a few days earlier. The hotel claimed this was due to a lack of prepayment, despite the fact that we had booked with the pay-at-the-property option.
The hotel never informed us in any way that the reservation had been canceled. What is even more concerning, the reservation was still shown as active in the Booking.com app at the time of our arrival.
Because all rooms were sold out, we were left without accommodation with two small children. At that time, due to a public holiday, there were no available hotel rooms anywhere in Miami. The manager, Mariano, tried to conceal the hotel’s mistake and shockingly suggested that we take a walk around Miami in the middle of the night with our children to look for another hotel.
As a result, we were forced to spend the night in the hotel lobby, waiting for a room to become available the next day.
This situation shows a complete lack of professionalism, responsibility, and basic concern .

The overall stay was satisfactory; however, compared with another nearby property (Smart Brickell Miami), several areas could be improved to enhance the guest experience:
•	Gym: The facility was smaller and less modern than Smart Brickell’s, which offered a better-maintained and more complete setup.
•	Room amenities: The room at Smart Brickell was more spacious and included a full dining setup (table, chairs, cutlery, and glasses), along with a modern washer, dryer, and dishwasher.
•	Internet: Wi-Fi speed and stability were noticeably better at Smart Brickell.
•	Late check-out: The fee here was $50 per hour, whereas Smart Brickell charged $25 per hour, offering greater flexibility.
•	Housekeeping: The sofa bed was not prepared, and no additional towels were provided.
•	Breakfast: Service ended at 10 a.m., while other hotels in the area extend it to 11 a.m., which is more convenient for guests.

Overall, the stay was comfortable, but there is room for improvement in amenities, service consistency, and overall value.

text.text:
The Indigo Hotel in Miami has a good location, but unfortunately my experience was very frustrating, primarily due to how a simple request was handled.

From the first day, I explained that I needed to use my room on the last day until approximately 2:15pm. I was told to ask again the next day. When I did, I was told it should be fine and that there was also a private rooftop space available if needed. On the day of checkout, I asked again and was told I could use the rooftop private room. Essentially, I asked about 5 times and was told it would be no problem.

When I went upstairs, someone else was already using it. Notably, each elevator trip took several minutes because the scanner system works poorly in the elevator, so going back and forth was time-consuming. I returned to the front desk and was told the rooftop room had been given to someone else. The manager then said I could use another hotel room until 2:30pm. I went up again — only to find someone else there with their belongings!!

Back downstairs again. There also seemed to be ongoing issues activating room keys properly at the front desk..

After multiple trips up and down (with very slow elevators), and repeated confusion, I was finally told I could use my original room until 2:30pm — which is what I had requested from the beginning. It’s worth noting that I repeatedly offered to pay for the late use of the room. While I stayed in the room (this is because I was doing a presentation to a large audience and needed private quiet space), 3 times someone tried to walk in to clean the room despite having “do not disturb” sign and having told the front desk.

Further, the AC did not seem to work and the heat is totally turned off. The gym is also very tiny. Hot water took about 10 minutes to heat up the first day.

While the location is nice, the lack of coordination, communication, and basic operational control made what should have been a simple request unnecessarily stressful.

The bad: OMG - warning, if you have a partner that snores, these rooms are like caverns or echo chambers. The no carpet, sparse furniture, allows the noise to bounce all over. Additionally, when you or someone with a nearby room runs the showers, you hear a clicking sound eminenting from the walls. Noise from the outside and hallway were also noticeable. This equated to no sleep for one of us. Two towels provided for two people. I have long hair, four towels should have been provided. This hotel skimped and it shows. Nothing special for the price point (I get it, it's Miami, gonna be expensive, but I've stayed in IHGs across the states that have been much nicer at lower cost).

text.text:
Two stars (and that’s generous).

I have stayed at Four Seasons properties all over the world. This was, without question, the worst service experience I’ve ever had at any Four Seasons — made worse by the fact that it occurred during a once-in-a-lifetime wedding weekend.

This property was chosen for a multi-day wedding involving over 150 guest rooms, private event spaces, and hosted events. Given the scale of the booking, proper planning and execution should have been guaranteed. Instead, the service failures were constant and inexcusable.

On the wedding day, the groom rented a private ballroom so his closest childhood friends could gather for a long-standing tradition before photos and the church ceremony. Clear instructions were communicated multiple times for the room to be stocked with liquor, mixers, water, ice, and food.

At 12:00 PM, we arrived to:
•	No drinks
•	No food
•	No mixers
•	No water

After repeated reminders, staff eventually delivered two bottles of liquor, a fruit plate, and an ice bucket barely large enough for one person, and told us the rest was “on the way.” It never came.

Over an hour passed with nothing. We then ordered 10 iced espressos.
Thirty minutes passed — nothing.
Another hour passed — still nothing.

With only 30 minutes left before leaving for the church ceremony, someone had to physically escalate the issue to concierge. Only then did the drinks arrive — nearly two hours after ordering — followed immediately by a check attempting to charge us.

Attempting to charge for service that took hours to arrive, after failing to deliver what was promised, was not only inappropriate — it was insulting.

The pool party later that weekend with 100+ guests was equally unacceptable:
•	Drinks took 30–45 minutes per round
•	Food took up to two hours
•	Orders arrived incorrect
•	Staff appeared overwhelmed and disengaged

Waiting two hours for a salad, only to receive it incorrectly, during a hosted Four Seasons event is indefensible.

This was not a “busy weekend” issue. It was a failure of planning, staffing, execution, and accountability.

Four Seasons is known for anticipation, precision, and excellence.
The Four Seasons Miami delivered none of that.

If you are considering this property for a wedding or large event, proceed with caution. The service did not come close to meeting the standards associated with the Four Seasons name — or the price paid.

text.text:
My experience with the hotel restaurant was extremely disappointing for a hotel of this category.

On two consecutive days — March 7, 2026 and March 8, 2026 — I arrived about 10–15 minutes before the official closing time of the restaurant (10:30 PM one day and 10:00 PM the next) and was not allowed to be seated by the hostess, who said the kitchen had already closed. However, this information is not communicated to guests anywhere.

In other words, the hotel advertises certain restaurant hours, but in practice the service ends well before that. At the same time, guests who are already seated are not asked to leave at the posted closing time, which makes the situation even more inconsistent.

The attendant suggested ordering through room service, which according to the menu operates from 11 AM to 10 PM. However, when I tried to place the order, I was again told that it would not be possible because the kitchen had already closed.

In other words, even within the posted hours, it is not possible to have dinner either at the restaurant or through room service.

Notably, the same hostess was on duty on both evenings (March 7 and March 8), and the exact same situation occurred both times.

For a hotel in Brickell, this kind of disorganization and lack of transparency regarding restaurant hours, room service availability, and the overall guest experience is quite disappointing.

As someone who frequently stays at Marriott properties, I was surprised by this experience and hope management reviews this policy and ensures that the hours communicated to guests reflect the actual service availability. This experience does not reflect the service standards expected from a Marriott property.

text.text:
Top notch hotel in the heart of Brickell! Service was immaculate and area was very safe even late at night. Hotel is accessible by the people mover across the street. Tons of shopping and restaurants nearby! Parking is plenty in the attached garage / it is only 30$ for self parking which I’d recommend since valet is 50$ and even if you want to go some place, come back and pay for self parking again, you will still come out on top since it is only 16$ for up to 10 hours!

Room was massive - we had a 1 bed, living, kitchen  and also a washer dryer in room and a large balcony. The room was serviced all days (except for one day and it was quickly resolved with a call to the front desk!) the one complaint about the room is that the tv’s were 20 years old maybe! In this era of digital streaming, these antique ones felt like a time warp!

The bathroom was also dated and the shower nozzles surely need to be cleaned since water went everywhere!

We had complementary breakfast thanks to Amex, it was hearty - the over night oats and French toast are highly recommended!

My first time staying here was last night. We had an after 10:00 pm arrival time into Miami. We were going to stay in the lounge however, it was already closed for the evening.
We were exhausted and decided to stay here since, it is right there in the airport and we could get some sleep.
We were greeted warmly by the young man working the front desk.  We got the King Room and they do offer military discount with ID.
We were checked in and had the key to our room in less than 5 minutes.
The only downfall to this room is how expensive it is. I do understand the reasoning why because it is in the airport and the convenience. However, it could be much more reasonable to match other hotels in the area.
The room was clean, and everything was freshly made. Our room was at the very end of the hall, so it did take a while to get from the elevator.
If, you don't mind the cost, I would recommend staying here just for the convenience of being in the airport. We were extremely exhausted and it came in handy for us. You do have to go back through security once, you exit the hotel. I didn't have any type of negative experience here.

text.text:
I wanted to be exited about this place but outside of the friendly guy working at the Starbucks in the lobby on 2/23/26 at 8pm this hotel is subpar to every other Hilton I have stayed at. Maybe the guy at Starbucks should be put in charge of the whole hotel. The $38 parking is an undisclosed scam.

We got to our room to find trash behind the TV. The remote control for the bedroom TV was missing. A big stain on our sheets and more. We called the front desk, concierge, etc. for 45 minutes with no answer. It took almost 10 minutes for the shower to get hot.

I can’t recommend this hotel. Stay at another Hilton property instead.

We also ordered food. As I said in another part of the review. Choose Uber Eats or DoorDash instead. 18% gratuity on everything. The food was average at best and they forgot half our order. Almost $100 for sandwiches fries and drinks is ridiculous.

Who has a pool and hot tub that closes at dark?  This hotel. When check in is at 4pm, You can use the pool and hot tub for 2.5 hrs. Zero value.

The rooms have multiple light switches that do nothing… so strange.

Still waiting on a tv remote. I’ll update if they finally bring it before I go to bed.

text.text:
Stayed here expecting a typical Hilton experience but was pretty disappointed.

First issue: the room never got cold, which is pretty frustrating in Miami. The AC barely worked and the room stayed warm the entire time.

Second: the pool situation makes no sense. The pool is apparently open to the public on Fridays, so when hotel guests try to use it, every chair is already taken. There were no towels available either, so guests basically can’t enjoy an amenity we’re paying for.

The closet handle in the room was broken, which just adds to the feeling that the property isn’t well maintained.

Service was also disappointing. The front desk staff seemed indifferent even with a long line of guests waiting, and communication was difficult since some staff members couldn’t speak English clearly.

Overall the hotel feels dated, poorly managed, and not up to the standard you expect from Hilton. The location near the airport is convenient, but the experience itself wasn’t worth it.

text.text:
Upon arrival at the hotel, we were told that no rooms were available yet, which was disappointing after traveling. Fortunately, the hotel is located near several markets, so we were able to pass the time while waiting. After about an hour, our room was finally ready.

Unfortunately, the experience did not improve. A repairman had to come to our room twice to address an issue with the air conditioning. During the first visit, he explained that the unit was frozen and said the thermostat should regulate within an hour. However, even after four hours, the room temperature remained at 75 degrees, which in Miami feels very warm and uncomfortable.

I later spoke with Linda at the front desk about the situation. Her attitude was very unhelpful, and when I asked if a fan was available, she acted as though it was a major inconvenience to assist.

My family and I have stayed at this hotel for nearly four years and typically remain for about three days after our cruise. Unfortunately, based on this experience, this will be our final stay. If our visit had been any longer, I would have preferred to spend it in the lobby rather than in that room.

text.text:
First off, the staff here is absolutely wonderful. Many  are bilingual, (hey its Miami) which makes things very easy for people who do not speak English as their first language. We did not have a single negative counter with any hotel employee during our stay. Quite the opposite. They were very helpful.

Onto the rooms. Many people have given the hotel a lower rating because they say the rooms are dated. At hotels that get this much use, you are going to have couches that get worn out, etc. etc., but I think people are mainly talking about the carpet. The carpet is very clean and does not smell at all, but it looks like it was probably installed in the late 90s early 2000s. The dark green in the downstairs made me feel like I was in an old movie, but it’s all super clean.  I will include some pictures for reference. Like I said though, everything is super clean and nothing smells so… Does it really matter? The furniture in the rooms is nice-  very clean not stained. I like the artwork and the overall ambience inside as well. The views from the rooms are amazing. The hotel sits on like a little island in a lagoon so you have great views of the water on almost all sides. The only negative about the hotel rooms… Where is the microwave and the mini fridge? Our room had a mini fridge in it, but we were told that we could not leave personal belongings in it and we would have to pay a fee to have one brought to our room???That’s pretty ridiculous. Even the cheapest of hotel rooms have a microwave and a refrigerator so that you can store leftovers and then reheat them. I would highly suggest they bring those things back. I think that’s probably also affecting their room score.

The amenities are top-notch. This is seriously one of the nicest hotel gyms you might have ever seen. I was actually able to get my full workout in. The only thing they don’t have is a bench press, and I completely understand why for insurance reasons. Maybe they could add a Smith machine in the future to help accommodate that, but the cardio machines are great and they have many of them. There’s a full barbell section, and they even have a leg press! Like I said, one of the best hotel gyms I have ever seen. I was actually able to complete my workout, which is so rare when I’m traveling. The pool outside is beautiful and they also have a kids pool and a hot tub. There is a little walkway that goes out into the lagoon where you can see some of the wildlife and look out over the water and it’s really lovely. The only drawback to the scenery is that the airport is right across the water, but you know what that’s the price you pay for convenience. The hotel shuttle runs like a clock until midnight or so. We had no issues catching ours. I will say go to level G, not level two like it says on the hotel website. There’s a long row of hotel shuttle pick ups, (like 22 of them) and you can stand at one of them and pick up the Hilton shuttle from there.

Walk ability can be a problem here. There is a grocery store .8 miles away, and I walked to and from that with no problem. Just make sure that you use the proper pedestrian crosswalks. Do not jaywalk here. That could have disastrous consequences. Most of the places that you’re gonna wanna eat at and stuff though, you’re gonna need a Lyft or an Uber. The taxis here are super expensive so I would highly recommend using ride share service.

text.text:
I recently stayed at the Pullman Miami, and I must say the experience was far below what I expected from a 4-star hotel of this reputation. For the price charged, the quality of the service and the room was underwhelming.
The room felt very dated and dark. Specifically, the beds were extremely uncomfortable—they were far too soft and felt like they hadn't been replaced in years. It was clear the springs were worn-out, making it difficult to get a good night's rest. Furthermore, there was no minibar and absolutely no instructions provided for Wi-Fi, TV, or hotel services.
Cleanliness and Service:
I was also disappointed with the housekeeping. While the bathroom was cleaned, the rest of the room seemed neglected during the daily service. It felt like only the bare minimum was being done.
In a competitive market like Miami, I expected a much higher standard of hospitality. Unfortunately, this stay felt like a budget experience at a premium price point. I hope the management addresses these maintenance and service issues.

The toilet paper was one-ply, which probably is cheaper for them, but then we used twice as much. The location was close to the airport and very convenient to restaurants, and stores like CVS, Walgreens, Burlington, and Publix, which we visited a few times since we forgot to bring some items. They have a reasonably priced shuttle from a third party that goes to the port terminal. Overall, I would stay here again before a cruise.

Took about 30 minutes to check in - only two clerks available with a line of about 20 to 25 people on a Saturday night (peak cruise passenger arrivals) including those on my bus coming in on the bus from the airport.

Room smelled like sewer gas - first thing you notice when you open the door and walk in.  Other reviewers have made the same comment.  It was persistent, and bad.

Breakfast not included.  It’s listed in the room amenities section but there is a little asterisk afterward saying it’s not included. Deceptive.  I overlooked the asterisk when I made the reservation and was unpleasantly surprised when I went down to eat.  I paid. The buffet in its entirety consisted of dry overcooked scrambled eggs, bad sausage, cold potatoes, an apple or orange, and white bread for toast.  Nothing else.  $27 for 2 people.

This place is overpriced for what it is.   I won’t stay here again.

text.text:
Online photos are misleading.
Starting with the airport shuttle, when I called and asked where to get picked up they told me anywhere between doors 1-15, we were at doors 12 and the bus WOULD NOT STOP. We were waving him down, there was another couple near us trying to catch the same shuttle and that man was sprinting trying to flag down the driver. He eventually stopped down at door 16 and only stopped for about 1 minute and started closing the doors as that man was still running towards him and yelling. Then we get to the hotel and as soon as we walk in we see the lobby is very run down and does not look like the photos online. We have to put down a $100 damage deposit which we didn’t know about. But we got it back do it wasn’t a big deal but not everyone would be prepared to do that. Then we got to the room which was not the room we reserved (different size bed) and it smelled weird. The door did not have the latch to lock it. Rust in the bathroom, shower tiles appeared dirty, could not get hot or even warm water in the shower (even tried waiting for a good amount of time). Breakfast is no longer included, and for people who drive themselves there, you have to pay to park in addition to what you paid to stay there.

text.text: We just stayed overnight between flights and stayed here because it is conveniently located near the Miami airport.   The room was clean and quiet, with a coffee bar/microwave/refrigerator kitchenette in our room.  There is an nice outdoor pool but we were there after it closed.  The shuttle service runs once an hour on the hour and even in traffic only takes 10 to 15 minutes.  Attached to the hotel is Old Tom's Sports Bar and Grill which has a relaxed atmosphere and great food. We had the wings and the steak which were both delicious.  All in all it was a very nice overnight stay.

Just checked in for one night since we leave for a cruise tomorrow morning. After a long start to the day, my husband and I decided to take a quick nap before heading out. When I pulled the blanket down, there were some stains on the sheets. I immediately called the front desk (no answer, the same as when I called from the airport to confirm the shuttle pickup location). I then went to the front desk. I was told someone would come in shortly to change the sheets. Someone did, but overall a very disappointing start to my stay here. I wasn't expecting anything wonderful from Ramada....but a clean bed and bathroom would have been nice. Definitely paid too much for this. Would not recommend.
Also, if anyone is reading this for an overall review of what to expect, not just one based on my negative experience, here are some thoughts.
Room is very small. Bathroom tight,  not super clean, the lobby smells very good (much like a resort), short distance from airport and there are restaurants and small stores (like CircleK) to buy snacks and drinks.

I’m begging you, do not stay at this hotel. Thankfully, we were only here for one night, otherwise we would have left. Check-in was easy, however, the online check-in didn’t work. Don’t even bother doing it, just wait until you get to the hotel. Next, we called ahead of time to set-up transportation to the port. They said it was $14/pp and that we had to book at check-in. Okay; not bad. We went to book at check in and they told us we had to wait until the day of the transfer. We then waited until the next morning at 7:00 am and went down to book it. Somehow it was full, but there was no one down there? Whatever, we took an uber.

The worst part comes from the hotel room itself. The rooms are DISGUSTING. We found hair everywhere in the sheets, and it wasn’t our own. The bathroom is tiny. You can’t even open the door all the way as it hits the sink. You can barely turn around in the bathroom. The room had an awful smell. When we went to plug our phone charger into the outlet, the outlet fell completely out of the wall. The lamps were sticky and gross. The overhead light didn’t even work. PLEASE DO NOT STAY HERE. SAVE YOUR SANITY.

text.text:
When we checked in, we were given a downgraded room. When we asked, we were told that the room we booked (edited: and fully pre paid for )was overbooked and given away. The first solution, we will give you two rooms for the two of you!  That made no sense. We ended up getting a room almost like what we booked, but not quite, and Im pretty sure it's a lower cost room. When we got to our new room, neither of the key cards worked, back down to reception.   Got in the room, and the pictures online are definitely staged, touched up pictures. Way more run down than I expected.
When you leave the front desk and head to the elevator, you are meet with a pungent odor of  musty mildew and stale air, and most of the hallways are the same, there is no air movement.

Now, for some other surprises. The pool is closed, as far as I could see, there is nowhere online thasts listed so if you looking for a hotel with a pool, nope!
Then the "breakfast"  they call it a continental breakfast, but bitter coffee and a muffin dies not constitute a continental breakfast. Even the front desk staff say, "If you want breakfast, go to IHop."  That's fine if we didn't pay for breakfast included.

It's definitely not worth the price we paid for the room.  I have to find a way to get some kind of refund.

I stayed here for two nights. I booked a room with two beds for 4 adults. The room had a kitchenette for cooking. We get to the room and we had 2 towels 2 wash clothes, no cooking utensils no plates no pots or pans. I go to turn on the light and the whole lamp on a pole falls on me. It was broken. I finally found the phone to call down to the desk. No dail tone .
The  phone doesn't work. I go down to the desk and the lady asks me what did I need, I told her all of my issues. She went & got a whole dish rack full of all dishes we needed and handed it to me like I could carry all these dishes to the room and unlock the door.  She offered no assistance or a cart to push them on. She never said my phone would be fixed or anything. I asked about my towels and wash clothes and she told me I would have to come back to get them. This place was the worst. The hallways stink. The breakfast was very limited. You even had to ask for a cup to put your coffee in at the breakfast. We asked for a late check out they said that was unavailable. I asked did they have a bathroom down where we would be waiting for our ride she said no. She told me we would have to go across the street and use the bathroom in a store or another hotel. This the worst experience I've ever had at any hotel ever.

The  phone doesn't work. I go down to the desk and the lady asks me what did I need, I told her all of my issues. I asked about my towels and wash clothes and she told me I would have to come back to get them. This place was the worst. The hallways stink. The breakfast was very limited. I asked did they have a bathroom down where we would be waiting for our ride she said no. She told me we would have to go across the street and use the bathroom in a store or another hotel. This the worst experience I've ever had at any hotel ever.

I booked this place via Expedia.com. Hubby and I were traveling to Miami from Atlanta on a late night flight. We arrived at the hotel a little after 1am. Definitely was not impressed upon arrival but we didn’t see anything alarming to catch our attention.

Check in was easy and quick. As we made it to our room we took notice of the dirty carpet leading to the rooms. Once we got inside the room - realized it was just mediocre. Definitely not how the reviews portrayed it (I am an “avid review reader”). The sofa/loveseat had very visible scratches in it (took pics & even called the front desk to let them know so they wouldn’t think we did it). Hard floors throughout so definitely make sure you have sandals so you’re not walking barefoot.

We were supposed to be in a queen size bed but it definitely looked and felt like a full size. The countertops in the kitchenette looked like they were newer but the room needs renovating/upgrading.

We didn’t see any washcloths so my hubby went to the front desk to get some. He came back and said, “they don’t have any”. So we had to wash with hand towels (I took a pic - definitely awkward & not appealing). There were cracks in the shower and it just needs to be upgraded. Shower head had rust.

Definitely not what I expected based off the reviews I read prior to booking. Did it do the job - YES! Would I necessarily recommend - NO! We just needed one night. It was close to the airport. Just my opinion - I wouldn’t pay the money to stay another night or come back.

text.text:
Sleep Inn Miami Airport is a very practical option if your goal is simply to rest before or after a flight. This is not a luxury hotel and it is not meant to be a vacation destination, but it does exactly what it is supposed to do.

The biggest advantage is the free airport shuttle. It was reliable and quick, and the hotel is only a few minutes from the airport, which makes early flights or late arrivals much less stressful.

The price is very reasonable for what you get, especially considering the proximity to the airport.

The room itself had everything needed for a short stay. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was clean, and having a desk, fridge, and microwave was very convenient.

Everything worked as expected, which is really what matters for a stopover.

Check in and check out were efficient, but this is not a place where you should expect extra amenities or personalized attention.

Overall, this hotel is a great choice for one or two nights when you need a clean, functional place close to the airport with dependable transportation. It delivers good value and convenience without unnecessary extras.

text.text:
Very disappointed with my stay at Best Western Plus Miami Airport North Hotel & Suites.
When I checked in, the room appeared like it had not been properly cleaned. The floors didn’t look vacuumed, there was dust and crumbs around the refrigerator, microwave, and under the nightstand, and there were visible spots on the furniture. Paint was chipped throughout the walls. Most concerning, there was debris next to the toilet, which raised serious sanitation concerns.
The second floor, where we stayed, is currently under renovation. I understand renovations happen, but that does not excuse basic cleanliness. Regardless of construction, the room itself should have been properly cleaned and maintained. It was not.
Management did send housekeeping after I complained and apologized, but the only compensation offered was 15%, later increased to 20%. For a room that appeared unclean and unsanitary upon arrival, 20% does not feel appropriate.
To make matters more frustrating, the booking was made through my credit card’s travel service using my card, so now I also have to contact my credit card company to sort out the billing.
This was not a minor inconvenience — it was a basic cleanliness failure. I cannot recommend staying here based on my experience.

All told, considering the price, this is a good value.

text.text:
Stayed here for a week for work, overall would recommend
Pros:
- bed: very comfortable
- Room: good size and decently clean. As noted in other reviews there is limited privacy in the bathroom due to gaps in the doors, but sliding the door to close off the bedroom area works fine
- Noise: very quiet, didn’t even hear a young family next door. Some traffic sounds but overall not noticeable especially with the white noise from the aircon. I see other reviews complaining about street traffic and airplanes, but this hotel is clearly located right across from the MIA runways and on a busy road. What do they expect?
- Aircon: standard, no issues - it can’t be shut off it always circulates, but most people like aircon all the time so that’s no problem
- Fridge: worked fine, I turned it to the coldest setting on arrival. Only microwave is in the lobby but again that was fine as I only needed it rarely
- Gym: decent, a few cardio machines and one bench with free weights
- Parking: free, lots of space in a convenient lot right behind the hotel

Cons:
- Shuttle: as everyone mentions, unavailable and unreliable! we had to uber both to and from the airport
- Elevators: only one was functioning, the other was out of service the entire time
- Breakfast: complete ripoff, $20 for sad looking eggs and cereal, along with burnt terrible coffee.
- Pool: a lot smaller than in the hotels photos and quite unwelcoming, since it’s at the main entrance and faces the busy road.
- Restaurant: the rooftop area is fun for plane spotting. The salads were good but the rest of the food was fried and tasteless

text.text: If you can afford it, go somewhere else!!Although the staff were nice and the location was literally a 12 minute drive to the airport terminal. The property itself was more than dated and not clean at all. I had got stuck in Miami from a missed connection and thought the smartest thing to do would be to get a cheap hotel near the airport. Although it was beyond their control for my trip. The shuttle never came and I ended up spending half of my room right on a taxi. (It only comes once every hour) I walked into the room and it smelled severely of bleach. So I thought well although not ideal at least it’ll be clean. I was mistaken. It looked as if they never really did an actual clean and they had just been doing a “cover-up “ job. Meaning doing things like painting over things instead of repairing. There were cigarette burns on the curtains, there was mould and mildew all over the bathroom. There was a zip tie on the floor underneath my door as if they had tried to unlock it during the evening. The structure was so old that every time somebody walked by my bed would shake. Sticky substances on surfaces. The staff were fine and perhaps doing the best with what they are given. But this particular location definitely needs more than an upgrade. I don’t usually leave negative reviews but if I had of gotten a tip off, I would’ve booked somewhere else and spent the extra 50 bucks and got a hotel where the shuttle actually came and I wasn’t afraid to touch things in the bathroom. All that said I unfortunately didn’t get to use the pool area but I walked in there for three minutes and it actually looked fairly decent… sorry to say days Inn I don’t recommend this property at all.

text.text: This is my second visit within 2 months at this hotel establishment. During my first visit l must admit, I was very hesitant, nervous and even scared. Why? I read the reviews first and it was so many nasty and negative reviews about the room conditions and how bad the staff treated you. I was imagining the worse things ever such as a roach infested room , dingy or dirty linen and towels. However, on that first visit, everything that I’ve read was completely far from the truth! I initially was going to have a negative experience, but that got quickly turned around then for the better. I ride a mobility scooter, and that day that I came the weather was very cold in Miami and rainy. It’s when we recently had a very bad cold snap in every part of the United States felt it. I waited over an hour for the courtesy shuttle to pick me up along with the host of other people waiting to get on. I was in conversation back-and-forth with the general manager, Miss M at the time, and she assured me that she was gonna allow her Driver to know to pick me up first and to be looking for me. When he finally arrive, I was bum, rushed by all the people getting on that bus. They saw me there as well and when I asked the driver, what about me he said he could not get me that he will be back in an hour because the bus was too full. I practically cried I’m cold freezing cold. I’m in a mobility scooter and unfortunately at the time I did not have money to take a Uber or a Lyft I called back to management clearly upset, but she turned things around immediately by saying go take a taxi and let the taxi driver know that we will pay them as soon as they get here.  I was very happy. Although it was just me the room that I had was a double room humongous very large room very clean very neat. That was something else that was debunked in my mind. Not only was the manager nice but the staff as well, very friendly and extremely accommodating. I feared going to their shuttle complementary ride to the port of Miami, which saved me even more money, of course, but I thought that I was only going to the same type of shuttle and get left again because of people going and filling up fast with luggage and everything But instead, they actually sent a huge charter bus like one of those Tour buses with the big big space at the bottom of the bus to put everything in which fit my scooter perfectly. Fast forward I arrived yesterday yesterday March 1 I called the hotel to let them know that I am here and once again warned them I have my mobility scooter. Miss S the other general manager worked there at this time yesterday and she called me and stated that the company no longer pick up mobility scooters immediately felt frustrated, but she said instead take a taxi and we will pay for it when you get here. An instant smile grew on my face and I absolutely love this place and every time that I have to take a cruise out of Miami this is where I will stay. I learned a valuable lesson and that don’t always judge things based on other peoples opinions, but truly try and get your own experience to develop your own true opinion. My opinion is definitely changed as I prejudged it prior to me ever visiting. I recommend this hotel for a couple of reasons for anyone to come to to travel. First and foremost, friendly, and accommodate staff, Second large spacious and very clean rooms with a very comfortable bed, Finally, the courtesy transportation from the airport, as well as the courtesy, free transportation to the cruise port, saving us a lot of money.

text.text:
Good budget hotel but I have some suggestions that could make it better.

Firstly the rooms are a great size and very comfortable and the beds are extremely comfortable. Perfectly clean.

Our hallway smelt very damp and like feet and there was a dehumidifier running that was quite noisy.

Location close to the airport so it’s convenient.

But the main issue we had is the breakfast. There wasn’t a single plant based or vegan option available. No soy or oat milk to have with cereal or coffee. So much disposable plastic as well- not even a proper cup or mug to take a drink from. So not very environmentally conscious but I understand not wanting to wash up or deal with that afterwards. I think there could be a better selection for breakfast in terms of some vegetables or like not sugary cereals- maybe some muesli or granola. Coffee didn’t taste great either.

But otherwise the hotel is fine!

text.text: I use Comfort properties exclusively when I travel, which is monthly.  I chose this property over the others because of its rating.  Checked in on a Sunday, checked out Friday morning.  All work related.  First negative was every night after working 12 hours, coming back to the hotel, I'd go upstairs only to find my key didn't work.  I'd have to go back downstairs and get it re keyed.  By the 3rd night, I was disgusted and the overnight worker set it up so I wouldn't have to do it daily.  I also had no hot water, and on one trip up the elevator I saw a professional looking woman who told me she was the properties HR manager.  I told her about the no hot water, by the time I went to breakfast, I was approached by the hotels manager as I entered the dining room.  She profusely apologized, took me to the front and gave me a one night credit.  That going the extra mile made what I had experienced satisfying.  She knew how often I stayed with Choice properties and thanked me for my patronage.  I usually don't make reviews but felt compelled based upon her professionalism.  So although the property wasn't ideal, the professionalism of the HR manager and hotel manager was above reproach

text.text:
I booked this hotel as part of my 40th birthday celebration, a trip I had been excited about for months. My cousin and I planned everything carefully for our group, and we arrived in Miami two days early expecting a smooth, relaxing start. After seeing so many recommendations online, we trusted this hotel would be a good choice. It turned out to be one of the biggest disappointments of the entire trip.
We had three rooms, and every one of them had serious issues. My bathroom was completely uncleaned — not just missed, but genuinely filthy. I went to the front desk immediately, hoping someone would take it seriously, but no one ever came. I ended up putting plastic bags down just so we could shower. That’s how bad it was.
My parents’ room was even worse. They had cockroaches. I reported it, and again, nothing. No room change, no apology, no urgency. All three rooms had a strong, unpleasant smell, and we had to buy air fresheners just to make the stay bearable.
The washing machines didn’t work either. Traveling with a toddler, I had no choice but to walk to a nearby hotel to wash clothes. And I wasn’t the only one frustrated — several other guests told me they were dealing with the same problems. The staff acted like none of it mattered.
Breakfast was the same every day, and the staff would start putting things away before the posted end time. On our last morning, they began clearing the area several minutes early, even while guests were still trying to get food.
This stay added stress to what should have been a joyful celebration. I would never recommend this hotel to anyone.

text.text: My experience with GM Shonelle Boucher was horrible. I arrived in Miami Monday night and was stuck there until I could get my 2nd flight to Savannah. Due to the weather issues, all rooms were sold out so I made a reservation at this hotel in Ft. Lauderdale. I took a taxi which took 45 minutes due to traffic and arrived at 11:45pm at the hotel. The GM immediately was surprised when I gave her my name and presented my card and ID. She stated she had cancelled my reservation 15 mins ago because I didn’t have a valid payment on file. I asked why I didn’t receive a call, she stated there was no number on file with the reservation. A BOLD FACE LIE. I explained I’m a Marriott member and travel a lot for work and I’ve never had this happen. My profile is complete with all my info and I have the app which was not showing cancelled. She then preceded to become more aggressive and  blame me. She stated there were no other rooms and I should focus on finding another hotel. The app was still showing a reservation, and I watched as others were coming in who stated they had just called for a room and she checked them in. I even heard a guy state his friend was on a plane and still planning to arrive but wasn’t sure what time. I then asked her about the cancellation notification because I never received an email and I know the policy, so this was not normal. She refused to show me on the computer where my reservation shows cancelled and stated I could not take a picture. She then called customer service and they verified my room was cancelled verbally. I asked for an email and neither of them sent proof that my reservation was cancelled. The GM became very upset and disrespectful. She stated she was going to call the police because I was trespassing and made fun at fact I didn’t have a room for the night. To Cancel a reservation when you know there is a travel crisis with sold out rooms and blame the customer is horrible service. This was a situation that could of been handled in 2 minutes if the GM was able to provide actual customer service.

text.text:
I had a disappointing experience due to a failure in Marriott’s reservation system and the lack of follow-through afterward.

I updated my reservation to a different date through Marriott’s automated system, but the change did not process, resulting in me being charged for two nights even though I only stayed one.

While the hotel property itself doesn’t need to assume all the blame, both the property and Marriott corporate failed to reconcile the error, despite my status as a Marriott Bonvoy Gold member. This was a system issue that was never properly resolved.

Because of this experience, I am reconsidering my Marriott Bonvoy credit card membership and will be sharing my experience with my immediate network. I would not stay at this property again when traveling to downtown Fort Lauderdale, and I strongly recommend confirming any reservation changes with a live agent.

text.text: Stayed 3 nights, joining my wife on her work trip to Fort Lauderdale. She'd stayed previously at the Delmar and had a great experience. Unfortunately, this stay was less than stellar. It seems the Element and the Delmar are sister properties, as they share many amenities and branding, communication, etc. The hotel is valet only, and they charge 5-star hotel valet prices. Our check-in process was slow and disorganized, and there was (I assume) a new employee at the front desk who was doing their new-hire training or some sort of training on the front desk computer, while a line of people waited to check in. The pool could be great, it's large and has plenty of seating (although the cabanas were closed and looked to not be used anymore) - but the seats are old and stained, the spot lights are damaged/broken and have duct or painters tape all over them, and the windows looked like they'd never been cleaned. The hot tub was covered with a wooden lid, as if it had been out of service for some time. The elevator situation is less than ideal: there's always a 5-minute wait, and on nights the rooftop bar is open, the waiting area is crowded, and it's clear they give preference to those going to the rooftop over their guests. The room was decent, but the shower was nice. The water pressure and the amenities provided were great. The in-hotel restaurant was closed for renovations, but looked complete, so not sure what was going on there. In each direction, the view directly next to the hotel is an empty plot of land ready for development - very bland with no vibe. Overall, 2/5 (and that's a stretch). Very disappointing.

text.text:
I stayed at the Element Fort Lauderdale Downtown and paid over $450 per night, which made this experience especially disappointing.

The elevators are absolutely terrible. It regularly took 5+ minutes just to get one. Because of this, I didn’t feel comfortable leaving my room to quickly grab breakfast or squeeze in a workout—it was that inconvenient. When I asked the front desk, they said all elevators were working, they’re just “very booked,” which doesn’t excuse the poor guest experience.

At check-in, I asked for water and was told there would be two bottles in my room. Instead, I found one empty glass bottle. By that point, I was exhausted and didn’t feel like dealing with the elevator chaos again just to fix it.

Breakfast the next morning was another disappointment. It was extremely crowded, and they had no plates, silverware, or cups available. When I asked, it took several minutes to get anything, and I was eventually given plastic silverware, which feels unacceptable for a hotel charging this much.

Overall, this was a very frustrating stay and not worth $450+ per night. Between the elevator issues, lack of basic amenities, and chaotic breakfast service, I would not recommend this hotel unless major improvements are made.

Book elsewhere for a 5-star experience; you will

text.text: Honestly if you arrived at this hotel choice like I did through the Amex Hotel collection, this really isn't it. I won't get too crazy into it, because no one wants to read a rant. A late check in (despite it being pased 4 pm). A shower that makes a screaming noise when in use that can't be repaired (DO NOT BOOK ROOM 1604) that vibrates the whole room. There was still garbage in the bathroom (despite the late check in "cleaning"). The elevators are NUTS. Not uncommon to wait more than 10 minutes for one. Also, the elevator inspections expired in 2024, just a heads up, there. Oh, and the wedding they booked pretty much took over every space, making our reservations feel overshadowed and ultimately unimportant. The "luxury" may be there in the price, but certainly not the details. You want a nice two day relaxing enjoyable stay with your significant other, this just isn't it. Oh, and as I write this, the vanity is smashing against the wall as my significant other is putting on lotion, because it isnt affixed to the wall properly. Oh, and two bathrooms lights are blown out. Lol. That being said, the majority of the staff was accommodating and lovely, doing the best they could with a sub par situation. So, kudos to them. Maybe in a few years they will iron this out, but for the price point, there are far better choices for hospitality.

text.text:
I recently stayed at The Dalmar to celebrate a birthday. I booked the stay through the American Express Hotel Collection and I was expecting a high quality hotel and level of service.

My expectations were generally met, until my girlfriend began to dig into the chicken skewers that she ordered at The Sparrow. She cut into the all the chicken skewers and found the insides completely raw. I spoke with Gustavo, one of the members of the hotel staff, and he offered to have the skewers remade and removed from the bill. But by that time, my girlfriend’s confidence in The Dalmar and the mood for the night had already taken a toll. Not to mention that the lobster fried rice and egg rolls that I ordered were just okay.

Upon check out, I spoke with the hotel staff to see if they would be willing to comp the entire dinner bill (roughly $100) for almost poisoning my girlfriend. One of the hotel managers, AJ, swiftly denied the courtesy and turned my first stay at The Dalmar into what will probably be my last.

Regardless, I would like to thank Rachel, Sasha, and Gustavo for their high level of service and the hospitality during my stay.

text.text:
Our experience at The Dalmar was good—though not quite great. The front desk, in particular, could use some attention. When you arrive at a place to relax, the front desk sets the tone, and being greeted with such a cold presence was not a pleasant start. Additional training on warmth, hospitality, and guest engagement would make a meaningful difference.

That said, we still enjoyed our stay and made the best of it. The beds were extremely comfortable, which we really appreciated. Unfortunately, we weren’t able to use the pool due to the weather, and I do wish it were heated—the water was far too cold.

In the lobby bar and dining area, the air conditioning was blasting to the point of being uncomfortable, so I would recommend bringing a sweater. However, I must mention that the waitresses were extremely kind, attentive, and truly added a positive touch to the experience.

The issues mentioned are relatively minor and ones I believe can be improved. Overall, we would consider staying again if we have another opportunity.

We’ve been coming to Fort Lauderdale for the past four years, and our stay at Riverside Hotel Las Olas was hands down our best hotel experience yet.

Our room on the 12th floor was absolutely amazing — breathtaking views, a spacious balcony, and the perfect place to relax and take it all in. We were celebrating a birthday, and the staff went above and beyond by surprising us with special birthday treats delivered to our room. It was such a thoughtful touch and made the celebration even more memorable.

A very special thank you to Merline and Larika, who were incredibly attentive to every one of our needs. They truly went above and beyond to make our stay fun, enjoyable, and safe. Their hospitality made all the difference.

The workout facilities were the best we’ve experienced — spacious, filled with every piece of equipment you could need, incredible views, and even a sauna. The pool area also offered fantastic views and was the perfect spot to unwind.

One of the things we appreciated most was the location — walking distance to everything on Las Olas, yet quiet and peaceful at night so we could rest without disruption.

This was easily our best hotel experience since we started visiting each year. We’ll absolutely be back!

This Hyatt Centric is absolutely outstanding.  The rooms are spotless.  The two queen beds we had were so comfortable and there were soft pillows that added to the comfort.  We had a beautiful room with chairs and an umbrella next to the pool.  Our “cabana” had an umbrella, small table and three chairs and was attached to our room.  The bathroom had a nice walk in shower and was spacious.  There was more than adequate storage.  We ate breakfast in the restaurant and all of the food was excellent.  Shannette took great care of us as our server.

Best of all, we were able to get our room early right after the cruise.  There is a $50 charge for early checkin but it is absolutely worth it!  The airport and the cruise port are a 15 minute ride away.  Fort Lauderdale cruise port is so much more convenient than Miami.   We definitely suggest that you stay at the Hyatt Centric before and after your cruises.  You will be as thrilled as we were to have a hotel with people who genuinely care about you being here.

text.text:
Vintage with a convenient location

We stayed at this hotel for two nights and appreciated its great location. It’s within walking distance of cafes and restaurants, making for a pleasant stroll. It’s also conveniently close to the train station (we took a train to Boca afterward) and just a short Uber ride from the airport.

The hotel itself is very vintage—old, but with a certain charm. However, it’s not for everyone. The rooms are small, and there is no elevator, so be prepared to carry your luggage up the stairs. That said, it seems well-maintained for what it is.

We didn’t have a car, so we can’t comment on parking.

Overall, we’d give it a solid 4 stars. Would we recommend staying here? If you're on a budget and need a location close to the airport and train station, this could be a good choice. Just keep in mind the vintage style and lack of an elevator.

text.text:
It’s cheap for a reason, which is okay, but they had horrible customer service.

I called prior to booking to ask about: shared bathrooms (whether it was referencing sharing with a roommate or sharing with other customers), the complaints about the AC units on their online reviews, the light exposure in the rooms, outside noises (there’s light construction near by), and if any of these are effected by which room I was staying in.

I spoke to someone who sounded like a younger man (I didn’t get his name), and he told me, in short, that my concerns were not warranted, and that it didn’t matter which room I booked.

As it turned out, it was not true.

They were willing to attempt to change my room to one with a private bathroom the next day, but the one night I stayed, the neon light completely lit up my room (as seen in my video at 2:30am), I had to share bathrooms with guests (despite expecting to have a private one), the incredibly loud AC unit ran inconsistently all night, and the construction nearby woke me up early in the morning (it was admittedly not horrifically loud though).

The hotel is fine for what it is, but I did not like being misled about what I was getting.

To make matters worse, the manager, Michael Omar Frazier, made accusatory remarks via email whenever I shared my grievances and asked (not demanded) if I could receive a partial refund for the remaining nights given I was misinformed about the hotel.

I was at a physicians conference and didn’t have the time to get into an email spat, so I attempted to call. Michael Omar Frazier was conveniently not around, despite me calling 3-4 times over the span of a few hours and him telling me that he would be in by 11am. I did happen to get the front desk to answer, and she said she would leave a message, but she first tried to tell me it was my fault for booking the wrong room, and that I just don’t understand how window units work. (And no, the manager never called back.)

Overall, just shameful place. It at least gave my colleagues a good laugh when I told them about my comedy-movie-bad experience.

text.text:
Arrived 9pm on a Saturday. Scheduled to stay until Monday. Went to my room, got ready for bed and was asleep by 11:30pm. Woke up at 4:30am to a cockroach crawling in my chest. I stripped the bed to see if there were more and I found bedbugs crawling along the perimeter seam of the mattress. I went downstairs to let management know but there was no one there. I called the number provided and no one answered. I called again and left a message a few minutes later asking for them to return my call. I put my belongings in a large plastic bag, tied it, and put it in the trunk of the car, parked in the sun, hope bf that would kill any bedbugs I left there with. Then I went to breakfast waiting for the call but I never received one.
I returned to the hotel at 8:30am and still no one there. I called one last time and no one answered. I left a second message at this time. I had work meeting beginning at 10am so I returned the keys and a handwritten message explaining the circumstances.
On my way to the meeting, I stopped at a store and purchased bedbug spray. I opened the plastic bag that was in the trunk and sprayed inside it until the can was empty. At the end of the day, I took all of my clothes and anything else that could be washed and took them to the laundromat. Washed everything in Hot water and prayed I wouldn’t take them home with me.
I called Hotel.com (I booked the reservation thru that site) and requested a refund. I sent the video of the cockroach and bedbugs. They reportedly reached out to the hotel and they were informed that they have strict cancellation processes and wouldn’t be refunding any portion except for $50 (paid $365 for the 2 nights).
It is suspect that Hotel Evernia spoke with Hotels.com because they couldn’t give me a name or copies of anything that was in writing. Possibly Hotel Evernia would have e refunded the money but then again, I left reviews, completed surveys, sent emails, etc and no one ever returned any correspondence. So maybe they did deny refunding the cost of the hotel.

We stayed at The Lofts on Clematis in unit 405 and had a great experience overall. The room was very clean, and we did not experience any outside noise during our stay, which made it comfortable and relaxing.

We booked directly through the website, and management was very responsive through email. At first, I did not realize that all you have to do is reply to the confirmation email, and that is how they communicate. Once I understood that, everything was very smooth, and they always answered quickly.

Self check-in was very easy. They mentioned that instructions would be sent shortly before arrival, and we actually received ours about 20 minutes before the 4:00 PM check-in time. The keypad entry worked perfectly, and everything about accessing the building and room was simple and smooth.

Parking was also easy. About a block and a half away is the Banyan garage, where we parked from Friday through Sunday and only paid around $20 total, which was very reasonable.

On Saturday morning, the farmer’s market takes place right outside and brings a lot of activity to the area until about 1:30 PM, which adds to the lively atmosphere.

There is a vending machine on the fourth floor. It does not have a large selection, but there are still a few items available if needed.

Before staying, I had read some previous reviews on Airbnb mentioning occasional smells, but I did not notice any of that during our visit. The lobby, hallways, and our unit all smelled very pleasant. It’s possible there may have been city sewer work going on when others experienced that issue, because during our stay in early February we did not experience any odors at all.

The location is extremely central. We walked to several nearby hotels, and although they were technically walkable to Clematis as well, they felt farther away and had fewer things happening around them. The lofts are definitely in a better, more convenient spot compared to those.

For the price and the location, I would absolutely stay here again.

Paying $700 per night at this hotel was extremely disappointing. The room itself felt sterile and cold more like a hospital than a luxury hotel,  with no view whatsoever, which is unacceptable at this price point, especially in Palm Beach.
Customer service was equally underwhelming. There was zero flexibility or accommodation for a late check-out, despite the high nightly rate and the hotel not being at full capacity. No effort was made to find a solution or show appreciation for a paying guest.
For a hotel that markets itself as upscale, the experience falls far short. Between the overpricing, uninspiring rooms, and poor customer service, there is very little value here. Palm Beach has far better options that actually deliver luxury, comfort, and hospitality.
Would not recommend.

I stayed at The Ben Hotel in downtown West Palm Beach for one night during a business trip, and it was an excellent experience. The hotel’s location is perfect — close to restaurants, businesses, and within walking distance of many local attractions. Despite being centrally located, it’s situated on a quiet side street, so there’s no street noise in the rooms.

The staff was very friendly and welcoming. The hotel itself has a trendy, modern vibe with stylish décor that makes it stand out. There’s a well-equipped gym and a rooftop bar offering beautiful views of the city — a great spot to unwind after a long day.

My room was spacious, clean, and comfortable, with all the amenities I needed for a business stay. Overall, The Ben is a fantastic option for anyone visiting West Palm Beach, whether for business or leisure.

text.text:
The room itself was great and the location was perfect. Unfortunately, the service was disappointing and, at times, very strange.

We arrived early on a Friday, and since our room wasn’t ready yet (which was understandable), the front desk took our phone number and said they would text us as soon as it became available. We went out and returned at 4:00 p.m., the official check-in time, only to be told the room was still being cleaned and would be ready shortly. We waited in the lobby until about 4:40 p.m., then checked again. At that point, we were told it still wasn’t ready, but they would “take the hit” and give us someone else’s room — which was a confusing and concerning thing to hear.

Although the room itself was very nice, we had requested a cot at the time of booking and it was not in the room when we arrived. After calling the front desk, the cot was delivered about five hours later — without pillows or blankets. We called again to request bedding, but nothing was brought up. Around 11:45 p.m., we were startled awake by someone knocking and attempting to enter our room with a key. It turned out to be housekeeping delivering pillows — still no blanket. Had we not engaged the deadbolt, they would have entered the room while we were sleeping.

We requested blankets again the following day and never received them.

On checkout day, about an hour before our scheduled checkout time, someone attempted to enter our room again — this time without even knocking. It was a staff member asking if we were checking out. We still had an hour left, so it was unclear why they were trying to enter the room at all, especially without knocking first.

The room itself was great and the location was perfect. Unfortunately, the service was disappointing and, at times, very strange.

We arrived early on a Friday, and since our room wasn’t ready yet (which was understandable), the front desk took our phone number and said they would text us as soon as it became available. We went out and returned at 4:00 p.m., the official check-in time, only to be told the room was still being cleaned and would be ready shortly. We waited in the lobby until about 4:40 p.m., then checked again. At that point, we were told it still wasn’t ready, but they would “take the hit” and give us someone else’s room — which was a confusing and concerning thing to hear.

Although the room itself was very nice, we had requested a cot at the time of booking and it was not in the room when we arrived. After calling the front desk, the cot was delivered about five hours later — without pillows or blankets. We called again to request bedding, but nothing was brought up. Around 11:45 p.m., we were startled awake by someone knocking and attempting to enter our room with a key. It turned out to be housekeeping delivering pillows — still no blanket. Had we not engaged the deadbolt, they would have entered the room while we were sleeping.

We requested blankets again the following day and never received them.

On checkout day, about an hour before our scheduled checkout time, someone attempted to enter our room again — this time without even knocking. It was a staff member asking if we were checking out. We still had an hour left, so it was unclear why they were trying to enter the room at all, especially without knocking first.

Overall, while the room and location were excellent, the repeated attempts to enter our room and the lack of follow-through on basic requests made for a very uncomfortable stay. For a property at this price point, we expected far better service. Unfortunately, we would not stay here again.

text.text:
I stayed at AKA for 5 nights.

From the moment I stepped into the lobby, I knew this hotel was something special. Just the lobby scent alone was truly incredible. The attention to detail in the decor was breathtaking, with opulent furnishings and a sophisticated ambiance that set the tone for an unforgettable experience. My suite was an oasis of comfort and modern style. It has everything you’ll need in that room it’s; its own tiny apartment with a dishwasher, fridge, washer/dryer combo, dishes, eating area, bed etc. Truly amazing

The service here was simply impeccable. Every staff member I encountered was genuinely warm, attentive, and went above and beyond to ensure my stay was perfect. Very resourceful and very sophisticated. Even the valet as well.

The hotel also gives you a $75 dollar credit to use towards the shuttle, the blind monk, or a.market. Which is all owned by them.

This hotel is in an amazing area everything is
walkable.

Make sure you read the full description when booking though, they may not be hidden fees to some but I was not expecting them (it did not make any difference as I loved my stay)
Everywhere here has paid parking, the hotel has a valet only parking with overnight costing you $45 every night you stay, however you may get your car as many times as you like. Down the street is $20 parking but you may not get your car out or it’ll cost you another $20.
They charge you a $100 a night fee for anything you may have broke or damaged within the suite, it does get refunded but this is an additional charge once you get to the hotel on top of the booking charge
And the last charge I noticed was a $39 destination fee per night that is also not included on the booking of the room this is a non refundable charge.
They will also charge you every time you get the housekeepers to clean your room, if you put your zzz tag on the front door they will not come in and charge you which is what we did. You can also tell the front desk you may not want housekeeping while you’re there to avoid that charge.

All that being said my stay was absolutely wonderful and I would a million times over come back. Just be mindful of the costs while going there is expensive due to the extravagance of the area. Thank you AKA for the truly unforgettable experience!

The hallways were surprisingly dark- I loved the idea of the design of the light fixtures that were in the hallways, but in conjunction with the dark wall color and the dark carpet, they did not provide adequate lighting. I could see where I was going, but it felt more like club or romantic restaurant lighting than hotel hallway lighting.

Our law firm recently completed an extended three-week stay at Hyatt Place, West Palm Beach/Downtown.  I cannot say enough about the exceptional experience provided by Hyatt’s sales team.  Director of Sales, Michael Haysmer and his sales assistant, Crystal Ramirez made planning the event almost effortless. Hosting a trial team of 12 attorneys and staff and setting up war rooms in an out-of-town trial can be a challenge.  Michael and his team made everything effortless from start to finish.

From the moment we arrived, the team demonstrated extraordinary customer service—consistently attentive, responsive, and genuinely welcoming. Every staff member we encountered went above and beyond to ensure our group was comfortable and well taken care of. Their positive attitude created an environment that felt less like a hotel stay and more like a home away from home.

The hotel itself is beautiful. The recently redecorated lobby is bright, modern, and inviting, setting the perfect tone each time we walked in. We truly appreciate the hospitality and the outstanding service provided during our extended visit. This hotel and its remarkable staff made our long stay not only pleasant but memorable. We look forward to returning in the future and highly recommend it to anyone seeking exceptional service, and a welcoming atmosphere.
