We are locals but stayed at this location because of a wine tasting it held.  We had dinner at Osteria and it was fantastic.  Their rigatoni in beef bolognese was memorable.  BUT, that was the only good thing we experienced.
I must say, it’s been a very long time since I have been completely disgusted and grossed out by a hotel room, but they achieved it.  The windows were absolutely filthy with huge chunks of mold/fungus/mildew so you could barely see out.  Then I discovered that the “stuff” wasn’t just on the outside of the windows, but also on the inside.  I was afraid to touch anything and normally I use the in room coffee pot, but given the fact that they couldn’t clean something so obviously filthy like the windows, I certainly wasn’t going to risk using something less obvious from a hygiene standpoint like the coffee pot.
When we went downstairs to check out the person at the desk asked if everything was okay and I said “no, it definitely wasn’t”. She said okay, have a good day and walked away. She clearly couldn’t have cared less.
We made the mistake of having breakfast at their restaurant before we left and both of us were very sick for the rest of the day.
I highly recommend picking a different location to stay at if you have the option to do so.

text.text:
We have a back-to-back reservation as part of our stay was with a group. At check-in, I confirmed twice that we were checked in for the entire stay, specifically verifying the dates. Despite this, on day two, our keys stopped working, we were checked out automatically, and I even received a receipt by email.
After getting that sorted at the desk, we returned to our room at 3 PM to find it hadn't been cleaned. We called housekeeping to ask for service and at least some toilet paper (the room was out). When I called 20 minutes later to ask for an estimated time, I was given a rude "lecture" that I had only called "29 minutes and 29 seconds ago" and that with 350 rooms, they would get to us when they get to us. It took a second trip to the front desk to finally get this addressed.
Additionally, the bed was fitted with a sheet that was way too small, which immediately came undone. I asked the staff to change it and was assured it would be handled, but I returned to find the same sheet still on the bed. At this point I gave up…
On the bright side, Tyrell at the front desk was very helpful, and the restaurant service was excellent. However, we have come to expect much more from Marriott.

I visited this place over New Year's Eve and I was not initially impressed. At check on they told us right away that the restaurant on site was closed for New Year's Eve and New Year's Day and so the have is $50 breakfast vouchers for our stay. What they forgot to say anything about was that The Bistro was a separate restaurant and that it was open!
My family was also given a room on the concierge level with lounge access but they also were not servicing that lounge for the two days that I was there so no hot food was available in there. Plus they seemed to be confused about the special holiday hours hours that they posted on the door of the lounge, access was unreliable.
Our room was nice but very cold and the heater didn't work. I called the front desk and told them about the issue and also asked for extra blankets and was told that everybody else was asking for blankets so they didn't have any left. They also said if engineering was available, they would send them up.... Nobody came the first night and we were huddling for warmth all night.
The next day I went to the front desk to complain and told them about my discomfort and they apologized and sent engineering up right away to fix the heater and housekeeping up with extra blankets.
This is not the level of service that I expect out of Marriott and this is not the level of treatment that I've grown accustomed to as an Ambassador Elite member. Being warm and informed could have made this a 5 star experience and I have other options while staying in West Palm.

text.text:
A Palm Beach Gem with One Noisy Exception
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐
We recently spent a few days at the White Elephant Palm Beach to get some much-needed "us time" while visiting family in the area. Overall, it is a lovely boutique property that captures the Palm Beach aesthetic beautifully.
The Highlights: Service & Style
The service here is truly top-tier. A massive shoutout to Junior, who was the absolute star of our stay! He shuttled us around in style and was consistently punctual, professional, and ready to answer any question we had. He made our logistics seamless and elevated the entire experience.
The Room (404) & Facilities
While the room itself was well-appointed and comfortable, we had a significant issue with Room 404. Starting at 7:00 AM, and again in the evenings, there was a loud, jarring mechanical noise that was impossible to ignore. It definitely disrupted the relaxing atmosphere we were looking for. If you’re booking, I highly recommend the hotel—just perhaps ask for a room away from whatever mechanical equipment is near 404.
Areas for Improvement
• Amenities: For a luxury boutique hotel, the beach towels felt like a bit of an afterthought. They were thin and felt "dollar store" quality—certainly not on par with the rest of the brand.
• Housekeeping/Maintenance: A warning for those with light-colored clothing: the black ironing board cover left smudge marks on my white linen shorts.
Verdict: Despite the morning wake-up call from the walls and the ironing mishap, we would still recommend the White Elephant. The staff (especially Junior!) makes you feel incredibly welcome. With a few small upgrades to the amenities and some soundproofing, this would be a perfect 10/10 stay.

I grew up in the hospitality business. My brother created the Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas and the Cafes starting in London. He also created Mortons im LA.

I wrote a book titled "Everybody Eats There" about the world's 100 most legendary restaurants and Arianna Huffington loved the book so much that she begged me to write for her when she owned the Huffington Post. I did this for four and a half years. It is there that I wrote about many great hotels. You can read the stories by going tova google search and putting in my name, Mara  Gibbs and one of the names of the stories such as The Beverly Hills Hotel. I have been doing radio for 7 years based on the book and huffpost stories.

I thought the White Elephant in Palm Beach was very nice. I loved the beautiful large bathrooms especially the great walk in shower with a hand held along with avrain shower.

I was disapointed that there was not a real swimming pool and a restaurant in house that offered more of a variety and later room service. As well as a later check out time.

The staff was wonderful especially a young man who is a newbie. He was particulary warm, friendly and very helpful. He never scoffed at any request. He in fact offered his help before I could ask. Every hotel needs a person like Johnwayne.

I would definitely return to stay here and really want to stay at the Nantucket White Elephant.

Thank you

text.text: This review is given by 2 senior couples. So take that into consideration. The check-in process was easy. When we arrived to the unit it had not been cleaned; however, after notifying Henry it was clean and smelling great within 2 hrs. After buying tons of K-pods we discovered the Keurig did not work. Since we were here for 7 days I feel that should have been replaced. The beds are comfy, the couches not so much. The 1st bedroom has an open ceiling to the family room so privacy could be an issue. The kitchen and dining rooms were nice and cool but the bedrooms and family room got fairly warm. Would have helped if the thermostat was adjustable below 70 or possibly supplied fans for these areas. The WiFi was extremely poor with lots of buffering. If you’re a tv watcher it will be difficult. The view of the ocean is beautiful but with all the noise you can’t enjoy sitting outside. The noise also bled into the inside! It was nice having 2 king beds and 2 baths. There was a luggage scale, which was very handy. The parking situation was great and very convenient. The pool and beach area were amazing and so relaxing. The exercise room was not impressive (2 machines were broken and 2 were rusted). I liked the decor of the unit and there was absolutely no dust on anything which was amazing!!! Kudos to the cleaning crew!

text.text:
Very disappointing stay – absolutely not worth the price

This hotel looks much better in photos than in real life. The room was very small, and the entire property feels extremely old and outdated. Everything looks worn out — the furniture, the bathroom, and the overall condition of the hotel clearly show its age.

The bathroom was in poor shape, and there were almost no basic amenities. No toothbrushes, no toothpaste, no toiletries — just a single small bar of soap. For a hotel charging this much, that’s unacceptable.

The air conditioner was incredibly loud. It sounded like a tractor running all night, making it very difficult to sleep.

The only positives were the friendly staff and a decent breakfast.

We stayed just one night and paid $477 with taxes, plus a $25 daily amenity fee that supposedly included transportation to downtown Key West — which we didn’t use at all. Paying around $500 for one night for a place in this condition is simply too much.

Overall, this hotel is seriously overpriced and not worth the money.

text.text:
Our stay at this property was good. The pool was nice, free breakfast was fully featured, and the room was a decent size and clean. The pricing was also in line with not being close to the historic area of Key West, but is still conveniently located with a short drive to the historic area and near amenities like grocery stores. The service provided was good too.

With that being said, this is not the normal Marriott experience and a dated property. Some updates like comfy beds were made in the rooms already. When we left, they were in the process of renovating the rooms a few at a time. The renovations didn't disturb us at all, though it would have been nice to stay in an updated room already.

Given that the pricing is substantially cheaper than in the historic area, I'd recommend staying here if you're budget conscience and need a clean, family friendly place to stay. But know that it will not match what you expect from most Marriott hotels unless the renovations are complete.

In terms of accessibility, they had a pool lift chair. We weren't able to use it because the battery was not charged when we tried to use it. So would recommend reaching out ahead of time so they can get it charged up. Our room was wheelchair accessible with an elevator on the property to get us up and it worked fine with an accessible shower and easy to roll up to the sink. The bed was still normal hotel height and not lowered so that was inconvenient but workable for us.

text.text: Checking in was easy, I did feel a bit rushed as I had wanted to make some adjustments, I was able to, but I had to almost talk over the front desk staff. The rooms were clean, but a tad small. Bathrooms were clean as well, but they were very very small. Beds were cozy. The rooms are great for spending minimal time in while you adventure. We had ordered French fry’s chicken tenders and nachos, over $60 for chewy chicken tenders, the fries were okay, and nachos that were a pile of chips with melted cheese on top. If you’re hungry I would recommend DoorDash. I do want to give a shout out to Shelly, I believe is her name if I remember correctly. So friendly and really made my day just chatting with her.

text.text: GREAT place to stay Key West for one or two people! It doesn't have a pool (unless you book the whole connected house), but it's a short walk to the beach, and you're in the Keys! Everything in the apartment works great. Comfortable bed, full kitchen, cute bathroom. I stayed there for a WEEK and loved it. Not to mention the amazing coffee place with the nicest people just steps away. They also offered free bikes which I used everyday, biking to the beach or down to Duval street. Everywhere else is a short drive or Uber ride! The studio is connected to the house, so you may hear the occasional talking from the other guests, but again, you're in paradise. I also enjoyed sitting in the little courtyard between the apartment and the house. Also, the host was great! She let me check in early because I had a big gap in my day, and when I realized the door connecting the apartment to the house was unlocked (ONLY because I checked in early) she came right away and locked it. Very clean as well. Offered tons of towels and beach items for use.. recommend.

text.text:
This was a mixed experience for us.
First, the studio was clean, quaint and in good shape. All items working properly.
The electronic door lock could be aggravating to use sometimes it would open other times took several tries.
This place is located in walking distance to most of the attractions and bars and beachfront. It is however located right in the flight path of both incoming and departure flights to the key west airport and the planes flying low! Must hear 30-40 a day, all day long. Also, this studio apartment must be subdivided with another apartment, so if you have noisy neighbors ( visitors) in the adjacent unit you will hear way more than what you want to. Unfortunately we had several screaming noisy kids and an equally loud parent( or chaperone) constantly correcting the kids. So it could be very early in the morning or late at the evening hearing them. We tried to stay out pretty much as long and late as we could to avoid as much disruption as possible.
Overall the value of the place is good, in comparison with some others we looked into. It's not beachfront by any means, but it's located in walking distance from almost the whole island.
It would be a stretch to say it's a perfect place and location,in comparison to some other rentals. But it was easy to find, free street parking, very clean and well stocked with towels, toiletries and a full kitchen utinsels , stovetop, microwave and toaster oven. We did breakfast every morning in the studio to save eating out so much. So if noise bothers you bring earplugs and enjoy the rest!

text.text:
I recently stayed at this lovely hotel  in The Meadows neighborhood of Key West, and it was an absolute dream. Tucked away in one of the most peaceful and picturesque parts of the island, this property offered the perfect balance of charm, comfort, and location.

The home itself was beautifully maintained with classic Key West architecture, lush tropical landscaping, and all the modern amenities you could need. The interior was clean, thoughtfully decorated, and felt like a true home-away-from-home. I especially loved the private outdoor space—perfect for morning coffee or a quiet evening under the stars.

One of the best parts about staying in The Meadows is the neighborhood itself. It’s quiet, residential, and filled with gorgeous homes and tree-lined streets, yet it’s still within walking or biking distance to Old Town, local restaurants, and all the Key West action.

Whether you’re looking for a peaceful retreat or a romantic escape, this Airbnb in The Meadows is a fantastic choice. I’d definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone visiting the island.

text.text:
This hotel may not have every modern amenity the big corporate hotels offer, but what it does have is authentic local charm, and that’s exactly why we loved it.

We stayed a full week and had a wonderful time. We didn’t even rent a car—we simply walked everywhere, and at 69 years old it was easy to get around from this location.

The hotel itself is older but very well cared for. Everything is freshly painted, clean, and clearly maintained with pride. There’s a saltwater pool with a bar, which became a favorite spot to relax.

One thing we really noticed was how attentive the staff is to maintenance and cleanliness. When we needed the soap dispenser fixed, it was taken care of right away. The pool area is washed down every morning, and we saw the pool bathrooms cleaned multiple times a day. In fact, we seemed to notice staff cleaning somewhere on the property all the time.

If you’re looking for a big, flashy corporate resort, this probably isn’t your place. But if you want something that feels local, comfortable, and genuinely well cared for, it’s a great choice.

Our advice: skip the expensive corporate hotels and support a place like this.  And if you’re someone who prefers the big polished chains, that’s fine—just go stay with the big boys instead of giving this place a bad review for being exactly what it is.

text.text:
We had a fantastic weekend stay at Casa Marina and genuinely wished we could have stayed longer. From the moment we arrived, the team made us feel incredibly welcome and well looked after.

Ronald at the front desk was an absolute star and went above and beyond to ensure everything about our stay was seamless. His attention to detail and willingness to help made a real impression and set the tone for the rest of the visit.

Christian and Lizbeth on the beach were wonderfully attentive and always nearby when we needed anything. Lea, our server at the beach restaurant, was warm, engaging, and made dinner feel easy and relaxed. Each morning Natalia in the coffee shop greeted us with such cheerful efficiency that it quickly became part of our daily routine. Cassie at the concierge desk provided excellent recommendations and thoughtful advice that helped us make the most of our time in Key West.

I also had the chance to meet Thom, the General Manager, who was incredibly affable and took the time to speak with us. He made us feel truly welcome, which says a great deal about the culture of the hotel.

I feel terrible that I cannot remember the name of our lobby bartender. He was from Moldova and was such a pleasure to chat with in the evenings. We also really enjoyed Gabe behind the bar, who was excellent. Our room was beautifully maintained, and every housekeeper we passed in the hall greeted us with a smile and a friendly hello.

The food was superb everywhere we dined, and the location made it easy to wander into town and explore Key West. I travelled with my girlfriend and her parents, and it proved to be the perfect setting for a relaxed family getaway.

We are already looking forward to returning. Thank you to the entire Casa Marina team for such a memorable escape!

If I'm honest, I don't understand the bad reviews about this hotel. We had almost perfect experience. Almost is because of the check in time, BUT the receptionists did everything they could, to make my experience better. Hotel was really full, the room wasn't available for early check in, which is fine, meanwhile we spend a bit time at the pool, but at 4pm, what is regular check in time, the room still wasn't ready. As apology i got a credit to spend in bars/restaurants there, which is great.
In general every single employee was really friendly, kind and helpful!
The hotel is amazing, the beach does have enough chairs and umbrellas for everyone. Also great, that they have two pools, one adults only and one family pool.
Valet parking guys are great and helping with luggage, opening car doors etc!
We had a breakfast at Flagler's, we ordered a la carte, but they also offering breakfast buffet. My kids did love they pancakes! And my avocado on sourdough bread was amazing! Also service was amazing!
We had a room in a suite wing, everything was perfect, really nice suite, clean and comfortable.
We'd definitely come back!

text.text: We stayed Sun-Fri end of February 2026. We found the staff to be attentive to our needs, rooms comfortable and in good working order with regard to plumbing, fridge, TV, etc. Bedding was nice, we received extra blankets within 30 min of asking. Drinks and food a bit pricey, but certainly within expected range for Key West resorts. We rented a pool cabana for 1 day, it was wonderful. Stocked fridge with waters. Sodas, mineral water, and a large fruit plate as well. Towels and chaise covers readily available and personal attendants as well. While the resort is located quite a ways from the "main drag" of Duval St and Mallory Square as well as the main Marina, our group (late 50s to 70 in age) we still walked everywhere and did not need to hire other transportation. Only a 5 min walk to the south end of Duval which then extend 1.25 miles to the other end by Mallory Square. It was very chilly the first 2 days but when at the pool bar-restaurant area, the staff brought out space heaters which made it very comfortable. They also have beach blankets to snuggle under at the fire pits. If you're looking for white glove luxury, its not quite here, but this is a beautiful resort and we will certainly be returning here.

Overall not satisfied with 5 star rating and the service and the room condition. We booked ocean view king room and they allocated a room which barely has any view in it and i had paid a grand for it. I asked front desk to give me another room and they provided me an upgrade of ocean view with balcony for $85/night. We have requested front desk to move our luggage from old room to new room (upgraded) and they left our selfie stick in the old room only. During checkout we told them that we are not able to find our selfie stick, they told us to create a lost item request and they will help us ship the item. When they found the item now they are asking me to pay for the label which is more than the value of item hence I would prefer discarding the item.

Rooms were pretty average and if you stay in 3 star hotel you'll get same room.

Overall, pathetic service. We requested to get our room clean and we were assured it will be done but when we came back our room was in same condition as we left it. Same experience in breakfast, I have requested an egg white omelet and I have been told that they can't do egg white as they don't have the material. I asked them if they have egg they can take the yellow yolk out and that will make it egg white. Common sense but the manager just came to me and informed they can't honour my request. Then I told them that you can't honour my request in a-la-carte but in your buffet live counter your chef is giving egg white omelet and at that moment the manager told me that they can honour my request. So they are not customer obsessed and not looking to solve the problem but just deny the request.

Overall the only good thing about this property is it's private beach and nothing else.

text.text:
This is our second stay here.  We stayed the first time in the off season of September and I would say it was not bad and not exceptional 3.5-4 stars.  I read a lot of the reviews before coming here again for December 2025 and I must dispute a lot of what I read.  The staff was exceptional, they clearly outlined all of the fees upfront (resort, parking, etc.). This stay was exceptional.  I read about the slow elevators.  What are people expecting, Empire State Building express elevators, they were fine.  We texted daily with housekeeping and they would bring us whatever we needed when we had the do not disturb sign on our door.  The rooms didn’t smell, the a/c worked fine, and the entire staff was excellent.  It was a great getaway from the cold weather!  It’s not cheap but I would recommend this place to anyone.  We had a phenomenal time.  We’ll be back again.

And as a side note we brought our small chihuahua with us and most of the staff knew her name when we walked by.  Great time overall!

The resort was beautiful, but when you pay top dollar you expect top dollar service . What’s a beautiful resort with trashy service? Trashy.

Noteworthy: If this is a Personal Intimate, Non-Business vacation, you may want to pick another resort.

The bathroom could use a little update but overall it was great! The people at the front desk were very nice. The only big negative was when I booked the room I spoke with a representative in Jacksonville and she forgot to mention I would need security clearance before entering the base. I arrived at the base at 4:30pm and was told I needed the security clearance at NAS Key West, about 10 miles away. But the security office closed at 4:30! The gate and base security at Trimbo Point was able to do the security check there but it took them more than 2 hours to do it. I do not fault them at all because I was told at the hotel I was lucky they did it. Thank you base security for your help. Overall it was a very nice experience! Shame on the person who do not tell me I needed to have a security check prior to entering the base and the time the security office closes!

text.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️

This hotel earns a three-star rating primarily due to its location. Outside of that, the overall service and experience were subpar. Unfortunately, this property appears to have become complacent because of its proximity to Universal Studios—a trend I’ve noticed with several surrounding hotels. Many of those nearby properties have since closed, while this one remains open largely because the location naturally draws guests.

That said, both the rooms and the level of service reflect complacency rather than guest-centric excellence. The housekeeping staff were very inconsiderate, frequently opening and slamming doors early in the morning. While the hotel has a unique and visually appealing octagon-style hallway design around the elevators, it unfortunately amplifies noise significantly. Sound travels easily, making it very difficult to get a good night’s sleep.

The breakfast buffet, which retails for $22, was extremely disappointing. The sausage was dried out, there were no eggs available, the coffee station was empty, and the tables were sticky. I’ve honestly received better breakfast service at a Motel 6.

Maintenance and upkeep were also lacking. Issues included a tub stopper that wouldn’t stay up and toilets that ran continuously throughout the night. Overall, the property felt worn and poorly maintained.

I was especially disappointed to have redeemed hard-earned Marriott Bonvoy points for this stay, given the quality of the experience. Marriott should strongly consider inspecting this hotel to ensure it meets brand standards.

text.text:
Stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton Orlando International Drive near Universal and overall it was a solid, convenient spot with a few highs and a few letdowns.

The biggest win was the service. Every staff member we interacted with was friendly, helpful, and genuinely welcoming. Check in was smooth, housekeeping was responsive, and the front desk team made the stay feel easy and stress free.

They’ve also added a new arcade, which was a fun surprise and a cool touch, especially if you’re traveling with kids or just want something casual to do at night. The heated pool is small but actually really nice and relaxing after long days at the parks. It’s clean, warm, and perfect for a quick dip. The room views are a huge plus too, we could see Fun Spot and EPIC Universe from our hotel. The self pay cafe is a great touch. You can always book Universal/EPIC/IOA things right in the lobby. Plus theme park shuttles offer a great, convenient way to get to and from the parks…

Now for the not so great stuff. The rooms are pretty small and feel cramped if you have a lot of luggage. The overall look of the hotel is dated and could definitely use a refresh. Biggest downside was the cleanliness details. The curtains in our room were noticeably dirty and stained, which kind of killed the vibe and made the space feel older than it is.

Bottom line, it’s a good budget friendly option close to Universal with awesome staff and some fun amenities, but don’t expect luxury or super modern rooms. Great for convenience and service, just manage expectations on the condition and size of the rooms.

text.text:
Aged, Musty, and Not Worth the Price

We stayed at Four Points by Sheraton Orlando International Drive expecting a comfortable stay based on the Marriott Bonvoy name, but the experience was extremely disappointing.

The room had a stagnant, moldy, almost cat-pee odor that appeared to be coming from the bathroom. With no airflow, sealed windows, and no balcony or lanai, the smell lingered and made the room feel damp and stuffy the entire stay.

The property is clearly aging. The carpet felt worn and old, the furniture looked dated, and the room had that humid, musty feel common in buildings that haven’t been properly updated. The bathroom showed signs of age as well, with lingering mildew odors and poor ventilation.

Soundproofing is minimal. You can hear hallway noise, doors slamming, and outside traffic from International Drive. The air conditioner was loud and cycled frequently, making it hard to sleep.

Other disappointments:

• Outdated interior and worn furnishings
• Damp, stale smell that never cleared
• No fresh air or ventilation options
• Thin walls and noticeable noise
• Bathroom ventilation issues
• Overall “tired” and neglected feel

Parking was $20 per day, which feels excessive given the large surface lot and available space. Hidden costs like this add to the frustration, especially when the room itself is already overpriced for what you get.

Pros:
• Convenient location near Universal Studios
• Easy access to International Drive dining and attractions

Cons:
• Strong unpleasant odor in the room
• Poor ventilation and sealed windows
• Aging property with worn interiors
• Noise and loud AC unit
• Extra daily parking fee
• Poor value for the price

We booked expecting a reliable Sheraton-level stay, but the property felt neglected and outdated. Between the smell, lack of airflow, and extra fees, it was not a comfortable experience — and we would not return.

text.text:
I used Choice Rewards points to book a complimentary night at this hotel, and the experience has been nothing short of shocking. The front desk staff checked me in on their system, but then refused to actually give me a room unless I paid a $150 deposit — even though other guests were being charged $100 or less. When I asked why my deposit was higher, I was given no explanation at all.

To make matters worse, they never cancelled my reservation in the Choice system. They marked me as “checked in” and told Choice I was already in the room, which is completely false. Because of this, Choice customer service believed I was accommodated, and I was left outside in the cold and rain with nowhere to go late at night.

I’ve been a Choice Diamond member for almost 3 years, and I have NEVER been treated like this. I called Choice multiple times for help, and I was hung up on repeatedly because the hotel was reporting that I was already checked into my room. Meanwhile, I was literally outside the property with my luggage, soaking wet and freezing.

The room is not double-booked, not unavailable, and not occupied whatsoever the front desk simply refused to honor my reward stay while still keeping me marked as checked in. This is extremely shady behavior and feels like the property is scamming Choice by claiming guests are in rooms that they never provided.
There was no compassion, no problem-solving, no attempt to help, and no honesty. Just refusal, runaround, and misrepresentation.

I have stayed at Choice properties across the country for years without issues, so I am genuinely stunned by the treatment I received here. I will not return to this location, and I strongly urge other Choice members to be cautious when booking this property.

The mini bar area was convenient, and everything felt well looked after. Overall, it felt like a place where people actually care, not just about the hotel, but about the guests. We would absolutely stay again.

Anyway, beside that, it was a great stay and would definitely come back!

There is nothing that I can say that could describe how pleasent the experience of staying here is. Upon the quick check-in with friendly staff, we found out that the door to our bathroom wouldn't lock. 10 minutes after calling the front desk, we had a brand new, working lock. The suite was very nice, and we had no shortage of coffee and hot cocoa with a coffee machine convieniently in the room. Unlike most hotels since Covid, there was daily housekeeping, and our room was always very clean. There were always enough towels, the showers water pressure was good, and the bathroom was overall very nice.
Beyond the room, all of the staff were extraordinarily friendly! I would not hesitate to stay here again if I am every in Orlando. Thank you so much!

Home2 Suites by Hilton Orlando Near Universal was a solid place to stay and did exactly what we needed for a Universal trip. The rooms were clean, spacious, and felt more like a small apartment than a standard hotel, which was great after long park days. Having a kitchenette was a nice bonus for late night snacks and quick breakfasts.

The location is a big win; super close to Universal, easy Uber rides, and plenty of food spots nearby. Staff were friendly and helpful, and the hotel itself felt calm and comfortable despite being in a busy area.
Overall, a reliable, comfortable stay with good space and a great location. Would definitely stay again for a Universal visit.

text.text: This is listed on Google as a 3 star hotel but it's somewhere between a 1 and 2 star hotel at best. Photos are misleading.  When I was dropped off, I immediately wondered if the Uber driver dropped me off at the right place. See attached photo and compare it to the Google images. Guy at the desk was nice and got me checked in. When I got to my room, I immediately noticed a pungent and unpleasant chemical cleaning smell that was almost starting to give me a headache. The room was also grimy and not well cleaned. I couldn't even stay in the room long enough to research alternative arrangements on my phone so I hung out by the pool area to look on my phone. About 30 minutes after checking in, I told them I needed to check out and declined a different room because of the strong cleaning chemical smell in the first room. I stood there and argued for 5-10 minutes with the 2 desk people and some random guy that seemed to know them because the hotel refused to refund the $75 I paid for the room. This is all in the midst of Storm Fern while I'm trying to get back home from a trip but stranded in Orlando indefinitely until flights get figured out and I already don't know if I'm getting comped for other additional expenses. So now I have to worry about $75 for a hotel room they I didn't use and would have had no way of knowing I would have needed to cancel until I walked into the actual room. Don't forget to look at the photo I included and ask yourself if it looks like it matches up with the photos they put online. Once again this is a 2 star hotel AT BEST.

text.text: After booking last minute due to a family emergency, my family including my sister, her husband, and their one-year-old baby  drove from Atlanta, GA and arrived around 2:20 in the morning. Despite the late arrival, everything went smoothly. The beds were extremely comfortable and the hotel was very clean, but the highlight of our stay was Marteen’s customer service.When I arrived, Marteen was assisting another group with an issue, and I immediately noticed how professional and responsive he was in handling their needs. When it was my turn, he quickly helped me check in. However, when we reached our room, we discovered it had one king bed instead of the two queens I originally booked.I immediately called the front desk, and Marteen handled the situation with great determination and professionalism. It seemed there may have been a system error and our original room was no longer available, but Marteen kept searching for a solution and stayed in constant communication while we waited in the room out of the cold.At one point, I stepped outside, and suddenly  heard footsteps running. When I turned around, it was Marteen personally bringing the key to our new room and apologizing for the inconvenience. His willingness to go above and beyond truly stood out. Marteen’s service was outstanding, and he represents the business exceptionally well. Professional, empathetic, and solution-oriented  all qualities of a great leader. I will admit this was not our first, second or third choice to stay here but because it was last minute we had no choice, now after experiencing 5 star customer service this is my 1st choice now! And where my family and  will be staying in Orlando moving forward!

text.text:
I start this review while sitting in a Dennys at 1:40am, it being the only refuge with some comfort of home. In short, stay away. Just pay extra for a competent hotel, like Hyatt. Don’t be like us.

At 10pm on our second night we attempted to return to our room. The lock refused to open.

At this time we returned to the front desk, the receptionist was extremely willing to help with our issue. He printed new cards and told us they should work properly this time, as the hotel just went under renovation and the new system is finicky at the moment.

We return to our room and the new keys were dead on arrival. We quickly return to the front desk and tell him about our issue.

The front desk man profusely apologizes and follows us to inspect the door himself. After he inspects the door he leaves to find tools to reset the chip reader on the door.

Poor guy returns with fabric scissors and desperately attempts to fix the door in 50* temps. After a good 10min attempt, he calls in maintenance!

Unfortunately, maintenance never picks up. There’s no overnight maintenance at this cursed property.
The on call manager was UNWILLING to pay for a locksmith or nighttime emergency maintenance. Genuinely astonished at this nonsense alone.

We then get lead to another room to cover us for the night. This room has a rough working toilet, rust (I hope) stains on the floor, dust bunnies and a mirror covered in specks.

The time is now 3:05am, I’m exhausted and exceptionally frustrated with this stupid hotel. Safe to say my final night in Orlando will not be spent in this dumpster.

Never in my life would I think about my vacation being ruined with such swiftness.

If you skipped to the end. GO ELSEWHERE.

text.text: Do not stay here, we just had an incident of people breaking into my parents room and stealing their stuff, luckily the police department has a fast response. I am told by the police that this has not been the first time at this hotel. The rooms have roaches, rust everywhere, and seems like no working secruity cameras. Again DO NOT STAY HERE UNLESS YOU WANT THE RISK OF YOUR STUFF STOLEN WHILE ON VACATION. Aside from the breaking and entering the room is not well kept. The bathroom handle is not screwed on all the way, the hook for the towels fell out of the wall while somebody was in the shower and there is rust all over the dirty floors. We have been talking to other people who stay here and apparently there have been other incidents within the last week alone. A man and his wife were sleeping and somebody had walked in, we assume with a key card since their door was locked. Management is not here and they cant do anything until the morning. They have not been helpful in the situation involving the cops and there is no security. The hotel staff was completely hands off with this situation and they dont seem to want to remedy anything that has happened. There is blood on the sheets from the people who broke in and the hotel almost didnt accomodate us, we had to raise a little hell for anything to happen. Do not book here, its unsafe. We are lucky we are with a big enough group to be able to handle an incident like this. There is a lady a few doors down with her 2 kids and i am so glad this happened to us instead of her. Scary situation that you dont want to find yourself in. Update; they had a master key card to access the rooms. We found it in the room left on the bed.

We just checked out this morning after a five day stay. We travel a lot, and our preferred hotel is the Hampton inn. So, we have been blessed to see quite a few locations. This hotel is an order build; however, I was very observant to see the attention to detail on its clean smell and appearance. It's very evident that the staff who work here are either held to a high degree of performance and or really take pride in their work ethics. I tend to learn towards both. we always travel with disinfectant spray and wipes. And thoroughly check the room out, the bed, bathroom etc. The room was outstanding. The breakfast was hot with nice choices and a clean setup.
Well, the icing on the cake was the front desk Clerk (EARL) we enjoyed our trip and yet leaving to return home our hearts was saddened to leave EARL. It's very hard to acquire awesome professional staff in any job field these days. The Hampton Inn has a jewel with this guy. Earl was so kind to us beyond the required measure. He would greet me every time I come down in the lobby or heading out by name "Mr. Carter this or that" always ensuring that our expectations are met and if we needed anything within his power, he would make it happen. We look forward to coming back to Florida if it's the Lords will. Without a doubt this Hampton Inn will be our location and hopefully seeing EARL once again we will never forget his acts of kindness. I must mention this I'm very observant, Earl is like this with all the customers(guest). SPECTACULAR

text.text:
While I appreciate the effort made by the front desk to accommodate my early arrival for a 2pm check-in, this positive experience was quickly overshadowed by severe issues related to room comfort and basic maintenance.
My initial room experienced a critical failure with the hot water supply. The water was lukewarm at best, estimated around 80°F (26.7°C). Maintenance was dispatched but the issue was not resolved; upon checking again, the water had become ice cold. I was moved to a second room just down the hallway on the same floor, where the water was again tepid, leading me to ultimately accept that functional hot water was unavailable at this location. Furthermore, the air conditioning in the second room was ineffective, struggling to maintain a temperature below 76°F (24.4°C) throughout my stay.
Beyond the climate control issues, the hotel's general condition was unacceptable. The rooms felt significantly outdated, featuring noticeable wear and persistent musty odors. The bathrooms were poorly cleaned, which is a major concern. The common areas contributed to the poor atmosphere, with hallways feeling musty and unconditioned.
The only true benefits of this property are its proximity to Universal Studios and the provision of complimentary, though unsecured, parking. As a frequent and loyal Hilton guest, I am extremely disappointed that this specific Hampton Inn location failed so completely to uphold the brand's expected standards of cleanliness and comfort. I will not be staying here again.

Horrible customer service, horrible hotel and they prey on out-of-towners as their business model.

The photos are of a third-floor room with a king-size bed. It’s perfect for a short family stay or a trip to the parks, since it’s very close to everything.

As you can see in the photos, the room has everything you need, just bring your own food. Everything was very clean, and I loved the herbal scent of the toiletries. The lotion, in particular, was wonderful. One thing to note: the showerhead is magnetic and detaches easily when adjusting it, so be careful. On the plus side, the hot water comes on instantly, which I really appreciated.

The sofa also converts into a bed, making it great for families. Breakfast is included, and the chicken was delicious. Although I didn’t get a chance to explore everything, I did see the gym and the pool, and both looked very nice.

I think this was one of the worst hotels I've ever stayed at in the Orlando area. I've been to Orlando dozens of times, but since this was a Universal Epic trip, I decided to splurge on the endless summer hotel. For $150 a night, I expected better, but I was sorely disappointed. The room was not clean, there were hairs from prior guests, dust, and thin blankets, even though it dropped to 40F in February at night, they basically only provide a top sheet. The walls were super thin, we could hear our neighbors on either side and despite me asking them to please quiet down, neither cared even though it was already 1 AM and I was trying to sleep. The shower was sad, with water that did not get hot and only stayed warm, at best. Our showerhead did not work properly and despite us asking maintenance, they never fixed it. Our toilet leaked and did not flush properly, but when they did come to address it, the maintenance man was condescending and asked us to display the ability to flush a toilet.
The dining room is the equivalent of a hospital cafeteria, overpriced and poorly serviced. I ordered a grilled cheese, which was served cold despite the scorch marks on it from being burned. My friend ordered the fish and it was so dry, that not even sauce could save it. I do not think anyone should be staying at this hotel at this price point, unless being able to be close to the parks is a deal breaker for you, then maybe you can withstand it.

text.text: Surfside Inn & Suites was great for the price. Our only complaint was how much noise you can hear in the room. If the noise doesn't bother you, I recommend this hotel. It's the best price for having a suite. The hotel is clean and all of the staff is very friendly and helpful. We arrived at noon and our room was ready, plus they gave us a one hour later checkout. It is not within walking distance to the parks, but the bus is very convenient and we never had to wait long. It's only about 10 min to get to the universal/Islands of adventure parks and about 15 min to Epic Universe. We ordered room service pizza and it was very good and fresh when delivered. We had a one-bedroom suite which worked out great for us. I slept in the bed that was by the front door and could hear every noise in the hall way and room's surrounding us. I had ear plugs that I could put in to block it out so it wasn't a problem for me, but something to be aware of - sacrifice price for noise. Despite the noise, I would stay here again. I like the Surfside better than the Dockside because it is a little smaller, plus the bus between the hotel and City walk/Universal Orlando/Islands of Adventure stops at Surfside before Dockside.

text.text:
I recently stayed at Cambria during my Universal trip and overall had a really good experience. The hotel feels very newly renovated, modern, and clean. For the price, it’s incredibly convenient and offers great value, especially if you’re visiting the parks and just need a comfortable place to rest. The staff were also consistently friendly and helpful, which made the stay even better.

There were just a couple of minor downsides. The hallway near the elevator on the 4th floor had a very strange and unpleasant smell. It was strong enough to notice each time passing through. I’m pretty sure management is aware of it because the hallway doors were kept closed the following day, likely to contain the odor. Hopefully that’s something they’re already working on resolving.

My biggest disappointment actually wasn’t related to the hotel itself. On the first night, our next-door neighbors were yelling and causing a lot of noise throughout the night until around 5 a.m. When I finally contacted the front desk, they responded immediately and handled the situation quickly and professionally. I honestly wish I had called sooner so I could have gotten more rest, but it was my first time experiencing something like that in a hotel.

That said, I don’t blame the hotel at all for that situation. The staff handled it exactly as they should have. If anything, it might suggest the walls aren’t the thickest, but again, the team responded right away when notified.

Overall, I would absolutely consider staying here again for future Universal trips. I’m not really a resort-style traveler, and this hotel checks all the boxes for a park-focused visit: clean, convenient, reasonably priced, and supported by a great staff.

The hotel itself was pleasant, and the beds were super comfortable. My room was very clean, and the shower had good pressure with odor-free water. However, the shower area had no place to put my own products, and the hotel’s toiletries felt watered down.
The air conditioner didn’t work properly. Every time I returned to the room, the temperature had changed on its own, and there was an unpleasant damp smell that made the room feel humid.
Parking was too crowded, but there were nearby parking options available. Still, there was no proper sidewalk or safe pedestrian access to get back to the hotel, which made it inconvenient when carrying luggage unless you parked right in front of the entrance.
The front-desk staff were inconsistent. Some seemed irritated, as if guests were an inconvenience, but one gentleman during my stay was very attentive, and the woman who assisted me at check-out was genuinely kind.
I also found the atmosphere in the common areas uncomfortable, the hotel had a strong curry smell in the halls. For anyone who doesn’t enjoy that scent—or the food—it’s something to keep in mind.
Overall, the location was perfect but not with a quiet environment, the room itself was comfortable, but with all these other issues, I wouldn’t stay here again.

text.text:
Edit/Update: I don't know why, but after the owners read this review,  their lengthy, condescending reply filled with excuses was deleted.

Well, every other negative review has a response from the owner with a short, condescending novel with excuses thrown in offering no solutions or apologies, so let's see if the pattern continues!

The room was spacious and the bathroom was nice (Steel Horse Room). The bed was uncomfortable- blow up air mattress and the thermostat was automatically set to 75°, which was adjusted after expressing concern, so that was good.

We did not experience the "warm welcome" that the other guests had expressed. The owner let his dogs walk up to us, clearly overexcited, seemingly out of control, then he quickly yelled at them calling them Dumb and Dumber (not their names) and telling them to sit. This happened twice while we were there for 2 days which tells me this may have been done for attention. We ran into both owners a few times and were never asked how our stay is going. There clearly lacks a hospitality background/experience.

The food was extremely lack luster. I promise it won't exceed expectations. You'd get more quality and quantity at a hotel. The owners don't seem to have great social skills so when the older gentleman sat with us and another couple, the vibe was a little awkward since he's not friendly. The kitchen looks disheveled (not clean like a restaurant) and there is a hint of urine smell in the living room that we're 100% sure the owners are unaware of.

The house could use some basic clean up around the yard and the porch- this would go a long way for first impressions when walking up. The metal sculptures are mediocre at best which is why you haven't heard of this "artist" until you checked out the place online first. There are 2 old vehicles and a run down boat parked where the guests are supposed to park. I get the classic appeal, but make more room for the guests and remove that broken down boat. It's starting to look like a scrap yard.

Thanksgiving night we invited my dad over to chat in the living room and at 10:04pm the lady owner comes out and speaks to us like children that the quiet time is 10pm. I understand that rule, not far-fetched, but her communication skills were extremely condescending. It's a holiday night, let loose a little.

There are many aspects of this property that could be improved with minimal effort, but unfortunately the owners invested in a restaurant while admitting they've never worked in the industry 🙃 This seems to take away from the B&B.

We booked based on the warm welcoming reviews and 4-5 star place, but did not receive any welcome and saw a 2 star set-up. With all the flaws we would've enjoyed our stay, but they were not nice people. Theres no point in trying to express these concerns to the owners since they've been so distant and short with us. I can garentee this review wont be responded with solutions or apologies nor will the B&B be improved, refer to other reviews for reference excuses and responses. A little hospitality would've made all the difference. We're clearly not the only ones that had this experience.

The room was spacious and the bathroom was nice (Steel Horse Room). The bed was uncomfortable- blow up air mattress and the thermostat was automatically set to 75°, which was adjusted after expressing concern, so that was good.

We did not experience the "warm welcome" that the other guests had expressed. The owner let his dogs walk up to us, clearly overexcited, seemingly out of control, then he quickly yelled at them calling them Dumb and Dumber (not their names) and telling them to sit. This happened twice while we were there for 2 days which tells me this may have been done for attention. We ran into both owners a few times and were never asked how our stay is going. There clearly lacks a hospitality background/experience.

The food was extremely lack luster. I promise it won't exceed expectations. You'd get more quality and quantity at a hotel. The owners don't seem to have great social skills so when the older gentleman sat with us and another couple, the vibe was a little awkward since he's not friendly. The kitchen looks disheveled (not clean like a restaurant) and there is a hint of urine smell in the living room that we're 100% sure the owners are unaware of.

The house could use some basic clean up around the yard and the porch- this would go a long way for first impressions when walking up. The metal sculptures are mediocre at best which is why you haven't heard of this "artist" until you checked out the place online first. There are 2 old vehicles and a run down boat parked where the guests are supposed to park. I get the classic appeal, but make more room for the guests and remove that broken down boat. It's starting to look like a scrap yard.

Thanksgiving night we invited my dad over to chat in the living room and at 10:04pm the lady owner comes out and speaks to us like children that the quiet time is 10pm. I understand that rule, not far-fetched, but her communication skills were extremely condescending. It's a holiday night, let loose a little.

There are many aspects of this property that could be improved with minimal effort, but unfortunately the owners invested in a restaurant while admitting they've never worked in the industry 🙃 This seems to take away from the B&B.

We booked based on the warm welcoming reviews and 4-5 star place, but did not receive any welcome and saw a 2 star set-up. With all the flaws we would've enjoyed our stay, but they were not nice people. Theres no point in trying to express these concerns to the owners since they've been so distant and short with us. I can garentee this review wont be responded with solutions or apologies nor will the B&B be improved, refer to other reviews for reference excuses and responses. A little hospitality would've made all the difference. We're clearly not the only ones that had this experience.

Nice courteous staff, cheap price, but DISGUSTING place. The sheets weren’t changed, but the guy at the front desk gave us fresh sheets out of the box when we asked for new ones. But that didn’t solve the problem. In removing the old sheets, we discovered the mattress was rotten, with holes and stains. We literally left the old sheets on and put the new sheets right over it in between to get us as far from the mattress as possible. The floors and walls were stained. The toilet was cracked. The single roll of toilet paper in the bathroom was stained with god knows what. We literally went out to buy a cheap roll of toilet paper and a shower curtain to lay on the floor of the tub. There were roaches, and the tub had actual dirt in it. Luckily it was just one night but I couldn’t even sleep, especially with the fridge making some crazy humming and rattling sounds all night.
The place is completely sketchy. There are clearly residents that live there, it’s definitely not just a hotel. I would not recommend for the life of you, staying here. No matter how cheap. Also, the pictures they have from ‘oyster’ are COMPLETELY staged. The rooms look nothing like that.
